papers.title: When Nonlocal Total Derivatives Are Not Variationally Trivial
papers.abstract: We study total time derivatives in infinite-order and nonlocal Lagrangian mechanics. In the formal infinite-order setting, such terms remain variationally trivial. For nonlocal functionals on trajectories, however, exactness in the form $L=DW$ is not sufficient to ensure a vanishing nonlocal Euler-Lagrange expression. We exhibit a smooth convolution-type counterexample.
papers.summary: This paper examines how total time derivatives in infinite-order and nonlocal Lagrangians can fail to be variationally trivial, providing a smooth convolution counterexample. It highlights that exactness of the Lagrangian does not guarantee a vanishing Euler–Lagrange expression in nonlocal settings.

papers.title: Galilean cosmologies in two dimensions
papers.abstract: Inspired by Carroll black holes, we consider the most general theory of Galilean dilaton gravity in two dimensions. We find generically that the solution space describes cosmological spacetimes. From a limiting perspective, these Galilean geometries connect the white and black hole singularities through the bifurcation surface. The latter turns into a Galilean extremal surface in the limit of infinite speed of light. We also discuss aspects of Galilean tachydynamics and find that the entropy is given by the dilaton evaluated at the Galilean extremal surface.
papers.summary: The authors construct the most general two-dimensional Galilean dilaton gravity theory and show that its generic solutions describe cosmological spacetimes with a Galilean extremal surface replacing the usual extremal horizon in the infinite speed of light limit. They also relate the entropy of these configurations to the dilaton value at the extremal surface, drawing analogies to black hole thermodynamics but within a nonrelativistic framework.

papers.title: A cubic closed string field theory
papers.abstract: The action of closed bosonic string field theory is non-polynomial, and for more than thirty years a no-go theorem of Sonoda and Zwiebach (1990) has excluded a cubic formulation with a single string field, a symmetric vertex and the canonical propagator. We evade it with a Hubbard--Stratonovich transformation and provide an explicit construction of a cubic closed string field theory at all orders. The transformation introduces an infinite tower of auxiliary $k$-string fields $\Sigma_k$, entering at order $g_s^{2 k - 2}$, which turn the vertices with four or more legs into kinetic terms and cubic couplings. The action is cubic, at most quadratic in each auxiliary field, and triangular: eliminating the auxiliary fields by Gaussian integrals recovers the original action order by order at tree level, under invertibility and kernel conditions on the auxiliary kinetic operators. The original gauge symmetry lifts to the cubic action with no new parameter, and we argue that the auxiliary fields add no physical state at generic momentum, wherever their kinetic operators are invertible. On the worldsheet, $\Sigma_2$ is an entangled two-string state: by an operator product expansion, the quartic form reduces to a gluing of two asymmetric cubic vertices dressed by the motion of the local coordinates and defined on states without level matching. We expect this picture to generalize to higher orders, defining a gluing of patches carrying $k$ punctures each. The string vertices, read as products with several outputs, satisfy an extended form of the genus-zero $\mathrm{IBL}_\infty$ relations, including operations with no input or no output, exactly when the string products form a cyclic $L_\infty$ algebra. Finally, we compare our action with the bar--cobar construction of Chiaffrino, Mamade and Zwiebach.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a fully cubic closed bosonic string field theory by introducing an infinite tower of auxiliary k-string fields via a Hubbard–Stratonovich transformation, thereby converting higher-point interactions into kinetic terms and cubic couplings. The resulting action preserves the original gauge symmetry, reproduces the non-polynomial theory order by order, and satisfies extended IBL∞ relations, offering a new algebraic perspective on closed string interactions.

papers.title: Anatomy of AdS black hole on-shell actions
papers.abstract: We revisit the regularized on-shell actions of rotating electrically charged AdS black holes of gauged supergravity via holographic renormalization and background subtraction, with a particular emphasis on the frame in which the radial cutoff is placed. For holographic renormalization, the asymptotically global AdS frame, recently employed in seven dimensions, works equally well in five and six dimensions: the renormalized on-shell action of the AdS$_d$ black holes with $S^1\times S^{d-2}$ conformal boundaries satisfies the quantum statistical relation, up to a parameter-independent Casimir term in odd dimensions, and thereby places the holographic comparisons that so far relied on this relation on a first-principles footing. Background subtraction, in contrast, fails to reproduce this result in the same frame; the mismatch, which we identify exactly in terms of the Casimir term and the counterterms, demands a criterion for the cutoff surface yet to be established. For precision holography, our results settle the choice of frame for holographic renormalization with conformally flat boundaries and delineate the ambiguities that remain in background subtraction and in holographic renormalization for boundaries that are not conformally flat.
papers.summary: This paper revisits the regularized on-shell actions for rotating electrically charged AdS black holes in gauged supergravity, demonstrating that holographic renormalization in the asymptotically global AdS frame yields a quantum statistical relation up to a Casimir term in odd dimensions, while background subtraction fails in the same frame. The results clarify the appropriate renormalization frame for conformally flat boundaries and highlight remaining ambiguities for non-conformally flat cases.

papers.title: Time Advances and Dispersive Constraints in Dressed Gravitational Scattering
papers.abstract: We derive a low energy group time advance in 4D dressed gravitational scattering at leading eikonal order with full soft dependence for a sharp dressing profile of finite soft scale. Dispersive matching of nonnegative absorption excludes the amplitude's analytic crossing with high energy boundedness. This reflects internal scales growing with energy via string diffusion in quantum gravity and high energy nonlinear graviton rescattering, coupled to soft clouds beyond leading soft order. Interference preserving joint detection of hard particles and coherent soft radiation may reveal the advance.
papers.summary: The authors compute the leading eikonal time advance in 4D dressed gravitational scattering, including full soft dependence for a sharp dressing profile. They show that dispersive constraints from nonnegative absorption forbid analytic crossing with high-energy boundedness, hinting at energy-dependent internal scales from string diffusion and nonlinear graviton rescattering, with potential observational signatures in joint hard-soft detection.

papers.title: Self-gravitating spinning mesonic tubes
papers.authors: Alex Giacomini, Marcela Lagos, Seung Hun Oh, Aldo Vera
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct new self-gravitating solutions for the four-dimensional $SU(2)$ Einstein non-linear sigma model and the Einstein-Skyrme model, both minimally coupled to the Maxwell field, which describes spinning pulsed mesonic tubes. These solutions are gyratonic in the sense that they are characterized by a propagation axis and possess angular momentum. The gyratonic solutions are described by a smooth matter distribution, which is free of curvature singularities. The maximum of the energy density is concentrated on a tube around the propagation axis. We first consider the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to General Relativity and the Maxwell field, constructing asymptotically flat, spinning, pulsed gyratonic solutions. Subsequently, we include the Skyrme term in the analysis. In this case, we show that in order to maintain the resolvability of the matter field equations, the spacetime must be asymptotically de Sitter. It is also shown that, despite the fact that the total topological charge is zero, these solutions possess a non-zero topological charge density.
papers.summary: The authors construct asymptotically flat and de Sitter self‑gravitating solutions of the SU(2) Einstein–non‑linear sigma and Einstein–Skyrme models coupled to electromagnetism, describing spinning pulsed mesonic tubes with smooth, non‑singular matter distributions. The solutions exhibit gyratonic behavior, concentrating energy density on a tube around the propagation axis while maintaining zero total topological charge but non‑zero local charge density.

papers.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
papers.abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $\Delta=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.
papers.summary: The paper develops a Gauss decomposition of the rational Yangian R‑matrix, interpreting the upper‑triangular factor U as a factorization twist that converts a non‑universal pseudo‑coproduct into the true Yangian coproduct. It shows that U can be computed as a Berry phase in a SUSY quiver QFT, leading to recursion relations for tunneling amplitudes that enforce the Yang–Baxter equation and exhibit wall‑crossing phenomena.

papers.title: Casimir Attraction and Repulsion in a Magnetic Domain-Wall Background
papers.authors: In\'es Cavero-Pel\'aez, Beatriz G\'omez-L\'opez, Jose M. Mu\~noz-Casta\~neda, Gonzalo Sancho-Garrido
papers.abstract: We study the one-loop Casimir interaction between two $\delta$--$\delta'$ plates in the fixed one-soliton P\"oschl--Teller background of the sine-Gordon kink. The transverse fluctuation problem is the Gaussian truncation of an $S^2$ sigma model, equivalently an easy-axis antiferromagnet with a domain wall, in which the plates exert no classical force on the wall. For $v\ge2|w|$ the fluctuation operators are non-negative, and strictly stable couplings, $v>2|w|$, also exclude zero modes, so the quadratic field theory is consistent at the fixed sine-Gordon mass. The background-dressed relative determinant factorises exactly into effective, gradient-dependent strengths of the two plates, and the sign of each frequency channel of the interaction energy is fixed by their orientation. Two identical, equally oriented, strictly stable plates switch from attraction near the kink to repulsion away from it under a rigid translation at fixed couplings and separation. The interaction energy and the force conjugate to the separation neither share their sign everywhere nor change sign at the same positions: there are regions of negative energy and repulsive force, so attraction and repulsion must be read from the force. For such plates with $w\neq0$ the force is repulsive at short and attractive at large separation, and the interaction energy has a minimum at a separation that depends on the position of the pair. For $v=1.05$, $w=0.5$ and $d=1.5$ the energy changes sign at $c\simeq-0.44$ and $2.63$, and the force at $c\simeq-0.30$ and $2.00$.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the one-loop Casimir interaction between δ–δ′ plates in a sine‑Gordon kink background, showing that the sign of the interaction energy and force can differ and that identical plates can switch from attraction to repulsion as they move relative to the kink. The study provides explicit conditions on the plate couplings and separation for stable, sign‑changing Casimir forces in a domain‑wall setting.

papers.title: Solving spectral flow in AdS$_3$: from covering maps to pencils
papers.authors: Sergio Iguri, Nicolas Kovensky, Julian H. Toro
papers.abstract: Strings in AdS$_3$ with pure NS-NS flux are described by the exactly solvable SL(2,$\mathbb{R}$) WZW model, yet correlators of winding strings, given by spectrally flowed operators, were so far known only up to three points. We obtain all of them, for any number of insertions and windings, in terms of unflowed correlators, proving the four-point conjecture of Dei and Eberhardt. The key ingredient is a pencil of rational maps from the worldsheet to the boundary which exists for generic insertion points, unwinds all insertions at once, and collapses to the covering map when the latter exists.
papers.summary: The paper derives all spectrally flowed correlators in the SL(2,R) WZW model by introducing a pencil of rational maps that simultaneously unwinds winding insertions, generalizing previous three-point results. This provides a complete solution to winding-string correlators in AdS3, confirming the four-point conjecture and offering new tools for studying holographic duals of NS-NS backgrounds.

papers.title: Solitons of the intermediate long wave equation with residue source
papers.authors: Yuto Ishii, Atsushi Nakamula, Soma Yoshida
papers.abstract: We revisit the bilinear formulation of the intermediate long-wave (ILW) equation by interpreting its principal-value integrals in the framework of Sato hyperfunctions. When the tau-functions have no zeros inside the relevant contours, the conventional source-free ILW equation is recovered. When zeros enter the contours, their residue contributions must instead be retained, leading naturally to a residue-extended ILW system with self-consistent sources determined by the tau-functions themselves. We introduce a residue index that counts the zeros enclosed in each analytic strip and use it to classify the resulting soliton sectors. The conventional elevation-soliton belongs to the zero-residue sector, whereas depression-solitons and higher elevation branches generally carry non-zero residue indices. Exact one- and multisoliton tau-functions are constructed, including mixed elevation--depression configurations with factorised two-body interactions. Their residue indices are additive and remain invariant during collisions, provided that no zero crosses a contour boundary. A Fourier-space analysis shows that the soliton spectra decay exponentially at large wavenumbers, with a decay rate determined by the distance of the nearest complex singularity from the real axis. This rate vanishes as an odd-multiple boundary between adjacent residue sectors is approached, providing a direct spectral signature of the transition between them.
papers.summary: This paper extends the intermediate long-wave equation by incorporating residue contributions from tau-function zeros, yielding a residue-extended ILW system with self-consistent sources. It constructs exact multi-soliton solutions, classifies them by a residue index, and links spectral decay rates to the proximity of complex singularities, offering a diagnostic for transitions between soliton sectors.

papers.title: $n$-Gon Correlators in $d$-dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the analytic structure of scalar one-loop cosmological $n$-gon correlators using an integrand-level reduction and a Baikov representation adapted to linear tube-energy denominators. At spatial dimension $d=n$, we determine the algebraic factors that normalize their local leading singularities to unity and construct explicit $d\log$ forms for arbitrary $n$. For the complete box at $d=n=4$, we evaluate an external-energy discontinuity in a collinear kinematic family and find a nonvanishing complete elliptic integral of the second kind after summing all time orderings. We also compare successive tube-energy discontinuities in $d=3$ and $d=4$, and relate selected tube cuts to the cosmological dressing representation. These results illustrate the importance of integration domains in determining the analytic structure beyond local leading singularities.
papers.summary: This work develops an integrand-level reduction and a Baikov representation tailored to linear tube-energy denominators for scalar one-loop cosmological n-gon correlators, deriving explicit dlog forms and normalizing leading singularities at d=n. The authors then evaluate elliptic integrals for the 4-point box in d=4 and compare tube-energy discontinuities in d=3 and d=4, highlighting the role of integration domains beyond local singularities.

papers.title: Canonical Commutation Relations and Poisson Brackets with Non-locality in Time
papers.authors: Yasu Gen, Hiroaki Matsunaga, Jojiro Totsuka
papers.abstract: We study the canonical structure of a string-inspired model in which the kinetic term couples fields at times separated by a finite shift $\sigma$, with a coupling $\lambda$ to a fixed background. From the boundary term in the variation of the action, we construct a conserved symplectic form and derive the positive-time Poisson bracket. Using the Schwinger--Dyson relation, we show that at positive time separation $s$ the commutator equals $i\hbar$ times this bracket. The canonical normalization $\hbar$ appears as a jump of the commutator expectation value at $s=\sigma$, which is equal time for shifted variables with a local kinetic term; for $0<s<\sigma$ the commutator vanishes for every $\lambda>0$. Hence $\lambda\to0$ at fixed $\sigma$ does not reproduce the free commutator on this interval, whereas $\sigma\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$ recovers the local commutator at every fixed $s>0$.
papers.summary: The paper studies a string-inspired model with a time‑shifted kinetic term, constructing a conserved symplectic form and deriving the positive‑time Poisson bracket. It finds that the commutator jumps at the shift time σ, so the non‑local coupling λ does not recover the free commutator for 0<s<σ, while the local limit σ→0 restores standard canonical relations.

papers.title: Simplicity of the Three-Loop Six-Point ABJM Amplitude
papers.authors: Hanyu Fang, Chia-Kai Kuo, Kai Yan
papers.abstract: We compute the three-loop six-point amplitude in planar ABJM theory using negative geometries. At this order, only a single bipartite chain contributes to the logarithm of the amplitude, and we find that its dual-conformally invariant integrand is locally finite. The integrated chain is therefore infrared finite and, remarkably, equals exactly $-\pi^2$ times the one-loop amplitude. Hence the collinear anomalous dimension, like the cusp, receives no three-loop correction. Restoring the disconnected products of lower-loop contributions, which carry all the infrared divergences, we obtain the full three-loop amplitude, fixed entirely by lower-loop data and the coefficient $-\pi^2$. These results reveal an unexpected simplicity of the six-point ABJM amplitude and suggest an iterative relation between its odd- and even-loop terms.
papers.summary: The authors compute the three-loop six-point amplitude in planar ABJM theory, finding that the only contributing bipartite chain yields an infrared-finite integrand that equals −π^2 times the one-loop amplitude. This leads to an iterative structure linking odd and even loops, with the full amplitude determined by lower-loop data and a simple coefficient.

papers.title: D(-1)/D7 bound states in supergravity
papers.authors: Gongrui Cheng, Klaas Parmentier, Thomas Van Riet
papers.abstract: We construct D($-$1)/D7 bound states in Euclidean type IIB supergravity motivated by the string-theory setup of Bill\`o et al., whose open-string description realizes instantons in eight-dimensional super Yang--Mills theory. Previous supergravity constructions either left unresolved issues concerning ten-dimensional Euclidean supersymmetry or relied on partial smearing to codimension one. We classify the local codimension-two solutions by showing that the supersymmetric field equations reduce to two holomorphic functions subject to a single complex constraint. The candidate bound-state solutions require complementary D3-brane fluxes, consistent with the D7 worldvolume analysis. A particularly interesting solution has constant dilaton and connects the vacuum at infinity to a controlled scaling limit in which the geometry becomes $\mathbb R\times S^1\times\mathbb T^8$.
papers.summary: The paper constructs Euclidean type IIB supergravity solutions describing D(-1)/D7 bound states, reducing the supersymmetric equations to two holomorphic functions constrained by a single complex relation. It identifies a special solution with constant dilaton that interpolates between flat space and a compactified geometry ∫R×S^1×T^8, and shows that consistent D3-brane fluxes are required for the bound state.

papers.title: A m\'enage \`a quatre without strings attached
papers.authors: Iosif Bena, Gongrui Cheng, Klaas Parmentier, Dimitrios Toulikas, Thomas Van Riet
papers.abstract: When two D-branes with eight mixed Dirichlet-Neumann directions cross, a fundamental string is created. This is the Hanany-Witten (HW) effect. In supergravity, the string shows up as an electric NSNS B-field sourced by the RR fields of the two branes. We show that two brane pairs, each of which would create an HW string on its own, can combine into a quadruple bound state with no HW strings attached. We explicitly construct a background with the fluxes of such a D0-D8-D4-D4' quadruple. Requiring no HW strings imposes a quadratic relation among the fluxes. We also realize this bound state as a supersymmetric solution of the non-Abelian DBI action of the D8-branes, whose Killing spinors match those of the bulk supergravity solution. The fluxed D8 stack acts as a domain wall between two supersymmetric D0-D8-D4-D4' backgrounds. Each background satisfies the no-string constraint, and the jumps in the fluxes give the charges carried by the stack.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a D0-D8-D4-D4' bound state that avoids the Hanany-Witten string creation by imposing a quadratic flux relation, and shows that this configuration can be realized as a supersymmetric solution of the non‑Abelian DBI action, matching bulk supergravity Killing spinors. It demonstrates how a fluxed D8 stack can serve as a domain wall between two supersymmetric backgrounds while preserving the no‑string constraint.

papers.title: Spectra and Central Charges of Gauged Curvature Squared Supergravities in Five Dimensions
papers.authors: Erol Aksoy, Cagatay Okyay, Mehmet Ozkan, Cemal Berfu Senisik
papers.abstract: We study the spectra and the central charges of off-shell gauged five-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supergravity extended by the Weyl squared, Ricci tensor squared and Ricci scalar squared invariants, and by their Gauss-Bonnet combination. Working exactly in the couplings and keeping all auxiliary fields, we organize the spectra around the maximally supersymmetric AdS$_5$ vacuum into supermultiplets. With the Ricci scalar squared invariant, the spectrum gains a long vector multiplet and is free of ghosts in a finite range of the coupling, while with the Weyl squared or Ricci tensor squared invariant, it gains a long spin-2 multiplet and always contains ghosts or instabilities. The Gauss-Bonnet combination adds no new modes: around its supersymmetric vacuum, the quadratic action is a rescaled copy of that of the two-derivative theory, and this fixes the spectrum of the Ricci tensor squared extension. We also compute the central charges $a$ and $c$ and the flavor central charge exactly in the couplings. The vacuum equation is $a$-maximization, and the kinetic terms of the massless graviton and vector multiplets are proportional to $c$ and to the flavor central charge, so that the critical points, where the massive spin-2 multiplet becomes degenerate with the graviton multiplet, are zeros of $c$. Finally, around supersymmetric AdS$_3\times\Sigma_2$ backgrounds of the Gauss-Bonnet extension, the two-dimensional central charges are reproduced by $c$-extremization, while the spectrum is generically not unitary and contains towers of states whose energies stay bounded at large Kaluza-Klein levels. In part of the parameter space, the tower of spin-2 multiplets has positive norm, so that the spectrum has no finite density of states.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the spectrum and central charges of five‑dimensional $mathcal N=2$ supergravity theories with higher‑derivative curvature terms, finding that only the Ricci‑scalar squared extension yields a ghost‑free spectrum and that the Gauss‑Bonnet combination reproduces the two‑derivative results. The authors compute exact $a$ and $c$ central charges, show that $a$‑maximization fixes the vacuum, and demonstrate that $c$‑extremization reproduces two‑dimensional central charges for AdS$_3	imesSigma_2$ backgrounds, while the spectrum generally contains non‑unitary towers.

papers.title: Radiation from scattering on multiple shockwaves
papers.authors: Tim Adamo, Anton Ilderton, Hannah Kingham
papers.abstract: It is well known that radiation produced by scattering an electron off multiple sources depends on the length of the mean free path between these scatterings. When this is sufficiently small, the spectrum is suppressed due to destructive interference, a famous result known as the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. This is usually modelled approximately, with scattering centres treated linearly (e.g., as screened Coulomb potentials), high-energy probes and soft emitted photons. In this paper, we consider a scenario where multiple scatterings can be computed exactly: charged probe scattering on multiple null electromagnetic shockwaves. Here, the amplitudes for elastic scattering and single photon emission can be determined exactly, for arbitrary kinematics, in terms of the shock profiles in the transverse plane. We use these amplitudes to compute the radiation density (doubly-averaged over shock locations in the transverse plane and lightfront time) in the regimes of independent and interfering scatterings. For shock profiles which are radially symmetric in the transverse plane (including the ultraboosted Coulomb field), we recover the known LPM suppression, albeit with more general kinematics. In addition, our setup allows us to consider the source-free case of multiple scattering on impulsive/ultra-short plane waves, where we find much stronger suppression of the spectrum in the LPM regime.
papers.summary: This paper derives exact amplitudes for an electron scattering off multiple null electromagnetic shockwaves, enabling a precise calculation of the radiation spectrum including interference effects. The authors recover the Landau–Pomeranchuk–Migdal suppression for radially symmetric shock profiles and find an even stronger suppression for impulsive plane-wave scatterings.

papers.title: Numerical Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes with Higher-Order Mass Corrections
papers.authors: Saad Eddine Baddis, Adil Belhaj, Hajar Belmahi, Yassine Hassouni, Maryem Jemri
papers.abstract: Inspired by noncommutative geometry and quintessence, we construct a new class of asymptotically anti-de Sitter black hole solutions characterized by a higher-order mass deformation term $\frac{aM^{n-1}}{r^n}$ involving two parameters, $a$ and $n$. Due to analytical difficulties, we approach the underlying thermodynamics through parallel programming simulations using CUDA codes. By considering models with $n=3$, $n=4$, and $n=5$, we numerically study certain thermodynamic properties, including the stability, the $P$-$v$ criticality, and the phase transitions.
papers.summary: The paper constructs asymptotically AdS black hole solutions with a higher-order mass deformation term aM^{n-1}/r^n and studies their thermodynamic behavior numerically for n=3,4,5. It analyzes stability, P-v criticality and phase transitions using CUDA simulations, offering insights relevant to holographic thermodynamics.

papers.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
papers.abstract: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.
papers.summary: This review connects the resurgent structure of topological string free energies to BPS invariants of type II compactifications, showing that Borel singularities correspond to integral periods of D-brane central charges and that Stokes constants encode generalized DT invariants. It also discusses how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations yield non-perturbative amplitudes and examines the correspondence in both local and compact Calabi-Yau geometries.

papers.title: Holographic dual of the 2d Ising model
papers.abstract: We propose a holographic dual of the 2d Ising model on a torus as the Turaev-Viro TQFT on a solid torus. The bulk spacetime is divided into the ``core'' region and the ``sandwich'' region. The core region prepares a defect state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on the topological boundary $\mathbb{D}$. The sandwich region computes the Turaev-Viro state sum $\langle\mathcal{D}|\Pi|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ between the state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and the state $|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ on the physical boundary $\mathbb{B}$. The fusion diagram (or string-net) $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{B}$ is given by the Aasen-Fendley-Mong construction. There is also a ``bedding surface'' $\mathbb{S}$ between $\mathbb{D}$ and $\mathbb{B}$, and the height variables (or Ising spins inside/outside of the domain wall) are naturally living on $\mathbb{S}$. The bulk spacetime is discretized by the 2-skeleton $P$ which interpolates $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{F}$. When the defect $\mathcal{D}$ is absent, the 2-skeleton $P$ ends on the bedding surface $\mathbb{S}$ and $P$ is interpreted as the bulk worldsheet of the string-net $\mathcal{F}$.
papers.summary: The authors propose that the 2d Ising model on a torus admits a holographic dual described by a Turaev–Viro topological quantum field theory on a solid torus, with a core region preparing a defect state and a sandwich region computing a state sum between boundary states. This construction realizes the Ising fusion diagram on the physical boundary via a 2‑skeleton bulk discretization, offering a concrete example of holography for a lattice statistical model.

papers.title: 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$: matching $A(k)$ in ABJM free energy
papers.authors: Stefan A. Kurlyand, Arkady A. Tseytlin
papers.abstract: The function $A(k)$ appearing in the large $N$ expansion of free energy of ABJM theory on $S^3$ is known exactly from localization. An earlier calculation of the 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, based on the standard KK spectrum on $S^7$, did not reproduce it. We identify a missing 1-loop supergravity contribution as that of the 3-form field fluctuations built from square-integrable harmonic 2-forms on Euclidean $\mathrm{AdS}_4$ tensored with $S^7$ modes, which are not captured by the KK spectrum. Adding it to the KK tower contribution expressed in terms of superconformal characters and applying the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ projection, the total expression simplifies, and its evaluation in a zeta-function prescription reproduces the expression for $A(k)$. We also apply a similar approach to the 3d ADHM theory whose M-theory dual is the orbifold $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_p$, which has singularity along the fixed locus $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^3$, supporting a 7d $SU(p)$ vector multiplet. Adding the localized KK modes of this multiplet to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-projected supergravity spectrum gives a 1-loop free energy that reproduces the ADHM localization counterpart of $A(k)$.
papers.summary: The paper resolves a mismatch between the 1‑loop supergravity partition function on (mathrm{AdS}_4	imes S^7/mathbb Z_k) and the exact ABJM free‑energy coefficient (A(k)) by identifying missing contributions from 3‑form fluctuations built on square‑integrable harmonic 2‑forms in Euclidean (mathrm{AdS}_4). Adding these modes to the Kaluza‑Klein tower, projecting by (mathbb Z_k), and evaluating via zeta‑function regularisation reproduces the localization result for (A(k)), and a similar method works for the ADHM theory dual to (mathrm{AdS}_4	imes S^7/mathbb Z_p).

papers.title: Schwinger-Unruh Interplay and Mode-Resolved Entanglement of Charged Scalar Fields in Rindler Spacetime
papers.abstract: We study pairwise and cross-horizon correlations of a charged scalar field in Rindler spacetime in the presence of parallel electric and magnetic fields. The transverse magnetic field produces Landau levels, while the longitudinal mode problem follows the charged-scalar Rindler construction with the effective mass $M_n^2=m^2+(2n+1)|qB|$. For a specified global vacuum in the negative-frequency sector, we obtain the outgoing four-mode Gaussian state and calculate logarithmic negativity and quantum mutual information for selected mode pairs. We find that the cross-wedge antiparticle-particle pair is entangled only when $q_2<\tanh r_U$. It can therefore become separable although its mutual information remains nonzero. The intra-wedge particle-antiparticle pair remains entangled for nonzero Schwinger squeezing. Using the Gaussian Schmidt decomposition, we show that the entanglement across the complete right--left wedge partition is carried by a pair of collective modes, even when the selected outgoing cross-wedge pair becomes separable. Using the Gaussian Schmidt decomposition, we show that the entanglement across the complete right--left wedge partition is carried by a pair of collective modes, even when the selected outgoing cross-wedge pair becomes separable. We discuss the Landau-level dependence and the limits of these mode-resolved conclusions, without identifying the vacuum-dependent mixing parameter with a detector temperature.
papers.summary: The authors analyze entanglement properties of a charged scalar field in Rindler spacetime under parallel electric and magnetic fields, deriving mode-resolved Gaussian states and computing logarithmic negativity and mutual information. They find that cross-wedge entanglement can vanish while mutual information persists, and that collective modes carry the full right–left wedge entanglement even when specific pairs become separable.

papers.title: Entropy and charge transport limit Mpemba preparation in holography
papers.abstract: We study Mpemba relaxation and its preparation cost in a holographic superconductor with full backreaction. At matched final energy and charge, boundary drives can reverse the ordering of the remaining horizon entropy after source removal. In separate numerical comparisons, some protocols reach a given tolerance earlier even when driving and waiting times are included. To examine the limits of preparation, we consider critical states that already carry a slow scalar field and exterior charge. Along the critical slow branch at fixed energy and charge, horizon displacement cancels the quadratic area response, leaving an entropy reserve of $O(\varepsilon^4)$ for an initial scalar amplitude $\varepsilon$. The same coefficient connects this reserve to the entropy advantage of the nearby superconducting equilibrium and the entropy weight of the slow tail on the normal side. This limited reserve constrains how quickly the existing field can be removed. For releases that suppress the leading horizon field and exterior charge, the preparation time grows at least as $\varepsilon^{-2}$ under horizon regularity and uniform radial control. Charge transport constrains the same covariant scalar flux that produces horizon entropy, raising the minimum flux cost and strengthening the time bound.
papers.summary: The paper investigates Mpemba relaxation in a fully backreacted holographic superconductor, showing that boundary drives can reorder horizon entropy and that preparation costs scale with the scalar amplitude. It derives bounds on the time and flux needed to remove the slow scalar field, linking entropy reserves to critical states and charge transport.

papers.title: Triple-Massive-Exchange Bispectrum of Quasi-Single-Field Inflation
papers.abstract: The triple-exchange bispectrum of the scalar quasi-single-field inflation model has resisted analytic evaluation across its full parameter space since its advent, despite rapid progress in cosmological collider physics. In this Letter, we solve it for general mass and mixing strength as a convergent double series, by applying the Mellin-Barnes representation directly to the mixed propagator between the massless and massive modes. The result is exact, non-perturbative, and physically transparent; the method is broadly applicable.
papers.summary: The paper derives an exact, non‑perturbative double‑series expression for the triple‑exchange bispectrum in quasi‑single‑field inflation using a Mellin‑Barnes representation of the mixed propagator, providing a convergent analytic result across all masses and mixings.

papers.title: Quantum and classical thermal equilibrium for probabilistic classical fields
papers.abstract: The time evolution of the probability distribution for classical fields can be described by the quantum formalism. For free classical fields the free quantum field theory arises as a subsystem. Different probability distributions for classical fields correspond to the classical thermal equilibrium with the Rayleigh-Jeans divergence or the quantum thermal equilibrium with the Planck spectrum. The selection of the Rayleigh-Jeans or Planck spectrum is not a question of fundamental concepts. It becomes an issue of dynamical selection once interactions are present. We compare the momentum dependence of the classical energy and field correlations for the classical and quantum equilibrium. This permits to decide which equilibrium is selected as a result of asymptotic dynamics by numerical simulations of the probabilistic classical fields including interactions. For free probabilistic classical fields we construct a general ``classical-quantum map'' between the classical probability distribution and the density matrix of the quantum field theory.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the time evolution of probability distributions for classical fields can be described using quantum formalism, establishing a mapping between classical probability distributions and quantum density matrices for free fields. It then studies how interactions dynamically select either Rayleigh‑Jeans or Planck thermal spectra by comparing momentum‑space energy and field correlations in numerical simulations.

papers.title: Harmonic superspace and Kaluza-Klein reduction
papers.abstract: We extend the Kaluza-Klein reduction procedure to the framework of harmonic superspace and apply it to the construction of off-shell superfield formulations of supersymmetric gauge multiplets. The reduction is implemented by a deformation of the harmonic derivatives by mass terms, while ensuring that manifest off-shell supersymmetry and Grassmann analyticity are preserved at all stages. As a first application, we reduce the free \(5D,\mathcal{N}=1\) Maxwell theory and obtain an off-shell superfield description of the BPS \(4D,\mathcal{N}=2\) massive vector supermultiplet. The resulting formulation naturally incorporates an analytic St\"uckelberg-type gauge symmetry. We then reduce linearized \(5D,\mathcal{N}=1\) Poincar\'e supergravity and derive the unconstrained harmonic-superspace action for the BPS \(4D,\mathcal{N}=2\) massive supergravity multiplet. The technical simplicity of the procedure stems from the structure of gauge theories in harmonic superspace, where the gauge symmetry is naturally encoded in analytic prepotentials and harmonic derivatives. The approach presented in this paper opens a direct route to gauge-invariant off-shell superfield formulations of massive higher-spin $4D,\mathcal{N}=2$ BPS multiplets. Furthermore, the resulting theories can be reformulated in $4D,\mathcal{N}=1$ superspace, opening the way to gauge-invariant off-shell descriptions of $4D,\mathcal{N}=1$ massive higher-spin theories.
papers.summary: This paper extends Kaluza-Klein reduction to harmonic superspace, yielding off-shell superfield actions for massive 4D N=2 BPS vector and supergravity multiplets while preserving supersymmetry and analyticity. The method also points to gauge-invariant off-shell formulations of massive higher-spin N=2 multiplets, with a possible reformulation in N=1 superspace.

papers.title: How to find regular black-hole islands in the swamp
papers.authors: Astrid Eichhorn, Pedro G. S. Fernandes, Verena Koeder
papers.abstract: An infinite tower of higher-curvature corrections is expected to lead to regular black-hole solutions. We assume that this regular behavior does not abruptly arise, but gradually builds up with each successive order of the effective field theory of gravity. In addition, we assume that the effective field theory comes with a single scale of singularity-resolving new physics. We translate this assumption into a monotonicity requirement for deviations of the metric functions from a Schwarzschild black hole. Under these assumptions, conditions can be formulated which trace the increase of ``less singular'' black-hole behavior on and outside of the black-hole horizon within the regime of validity of the effective field theory. These conditions constrain the effective field theory coefficients. To exemplify this construction, we motivate five specific conditions and find a corresponding island of black hole regularity conditions at order eight in the effective field theory. We also explore whether string theory as well as asymptotically safe gravity lie on this island.
papers.summary: The authors argue that an infinite tower of higher‑curvature corrections should gradually smooth out black‑hole singularities, formalizing this with a monotonicity condition on metric deviations from Schwarzschild. They then derive constraints on EFT coefficients, identify an “island” of regular solutions at eighth order, and test whether string theory or asymptotically safe gravity lie inside this island.

papers.title: Swing Surfaces in AdS/CFT
papers.abstract: We study holographic entanglement entropy in the flat limit of AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, and clarify the relation between Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces and the swing surfaces proposed for flat-space holography. We show that the ordinary RT formula does not admit a well-defined flat-space limit and connect this to subtleties of the state-operator map in the flat limit. We then construct an AdS$_3$ uplift of the swing prescription and develop its corresponding information-theoretic interpretation through two complementary approaches. First, we show that the swing surface length computes the mutual information between suitably chosen nearly null boundary intervals in a special class of pure CFT states. The gravity interpretation of this result involves scattering processes which take place deep inside of the AdS$_3$ bulk. Second, we reduce the problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation for swing surfaces to the more general problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation of black hole inner horizons in holography.
papers.summary: The paper extends the Ryu–Takayanagi prescription to the flat limit of AdS₃/CFT₂ by introducing swing surfaces, showing that their length captures mutual information between nearly null boundary intervals in special pure CFT states. It further links this construction to scattering in the bulk and suggests that swing surfaces may provide an information-theoretic understanding of black hole inner horizons.

papers.title: $\alpha'^2$-corrections to the bosonic string from an action-level double copy map
papers.authors: Eric Lescano, Agustina Pereyra Grau, Jes\'us A. Rodr\'iguez
papers.abstract: The low-energy effective action of the bosonic string contains higher-derivative corrections of the form Riem$^2$ and Riem$^3$ to the Einstein--Hilbert action, together with the associated Kalb--Ramond couplings. We construct an action-level double copy description of these corrections up to cubic order in the fields. Two ingredients are required: a higher-derivative gauge-theory Lagrangian, which up to field redefinitions is controlled by a single $F^3$ coupling, and a deformation of the color-to-kinematics replacement of the structure constants by the corresponding three-momentum tensor. We show that no higher-derivative gauge-theory operator can produce the Riem$^3$ vertex with the standard replacement rule, and that the matching conditions for the gauge-theory coupling and the deformation of the map admit a unique solution, a double root, which renders the cubic action left--right symmetric, of the form $(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)\otimes(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)$. Without further input, the resulting map reproduces the cubic $\mathrm{Riem}\,H^2$ coupling of the bosonic string at order $\alpha'$, the absence of six-derivative cubic Kalb--Ramond couplings at order $\alpha'^2$, and the absence of interactions odd in the Kalb--Ramond field. The comparison is performed in transverse-traceless gauge, up to field redefinitions.
papers.summary: This work constructs an action-level double-copy map for the $alpha'^2$ corrections of the bosonic string, reproducing the Riemann-squared and Riemann-cubed terms together with Kalb–Ramond couplings up to cubic order. By deforming the color-to-kinematics replacement and introducing a single $F^3$ gauge-theory operator, the authors obtain a unique left–right symmetric double-copy structure that matches the bosonic string’s cubic interactions while forbidding odd Kalb–Ramond couplings.

papers.title: Cosmological correlators and kinematic flow on complex Hartle-Hawking saddles
papers.abstract: The Lorentzian gravitational path integral over homogeneous and isotropic metrics in a closed universe with positive cosmological constant is dominated by complex saddle points, such as the Hartle-Hawking saddles. We ask how to compute cosmological correlators on such complex backgrounds, and how they respond to the shifts of the kinematic variables---the kinematic flow---without tracking the bulk time evolution explicitly. We, specifically, study a conformally coupled scalar test field with a cubic interaction around these saddles. We find that the wave function coefficients can be written as discrete spectral sums with the summands containing the corresponding coefficients in the Einstein static universe, which are obtainable in analogy with the polytopes program for flat spacetime. Whereas the wave function coefficients of the flat FLRW case are given by integrals over shifted kinematics, the discrete spectrum on the three-sphere for Hartle-Hawking saddles produces sums. We identify the coefficients, which depend on the final hypersurface through a phase fixed by its size, with Srivastava-Daoust multi-variable hypergeometric functions. They satisfy recursion relations for any number of sites, under which the sums collapse into rational functions. For the one- and two-site Feynman-Witten tree diagrams, we derive difference equations in the kinematic variables which close on a finite set of sums, giving a discrete kinematic flow. The transformation matrices are upper triangular with rational elements, and satisfy a consistency condition which makes the flow path independent. We then obtain the two-, three- and four-point cosmological correlators. At the late-time conformal boundary, we derive an explicit difference equation for the four-point function.
papers.summary: The authors compute cosmological correlators on complex Hartle-Hawking saddles by expressing wave function coefficients as discrete spectral sums over the three-sphere, which collapse into rational functions via recursion relations. They derive difference equations for one- and two-site tree diagrams and obtain explicit four-point correlators, revealing a discrete kinematic flow independent of bulk time evolution.

papers.title: Cosmological Dressing Rules for Massive Scalars
papers.authors: Jonathan Gr\"afe, Matthias Nowinski, Ivo Sachs, Siva Pawan Venna
papers.abstract: The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation of de Sitter correlation functions comes in different guises including harmonic analysis and dressed flat space correlators. We observe that these are equivalent spectral representations of the same Sturm-Liouville problem. Starting from the latter we derive dressing rules for scalar fields of arbitrary mass with auxiliary propagators in the form of Euler integrals that are accessible to flat space diagrammatic tools.
papers.summary: The paper develops a unified spectral representation of de Sitter Schwinger‑Keldysh correlators by recasting them as solutions to a Sturm‑Liouville problem, yielding explicit dressing rules for massive scalar fields in terms of Euler integrals. These results provide a bridge between curved‑space cosmological correlators and flat‑space diagrammatic techniques, offering new tools for computing higher‑point functions in de Sitter holography.

papers.title: Subsystem Flow: Quantum Error Correction, Petz Recovery, and Ergodic Inclusions
papers.authors: Yidong Chen, Nima Lashkari, Kwing Lam Leung
papers.abstract: In quantum error correction (QEC), the goal is to engineer an encoding that protects logical information against the erasure of a physical subsystem. In local many-body quantum systems, by contrast, nature provides a subsystem inclusion $\mN\subset \mM$ in a fixed reference state $\ket{\Omega}$. Asking whether the inclusion admits a reference-preserving code that protects subsystem $\mN$ against erasure of the complement is equivalent to asking whether $\mN$ is preserved under the modular dynamics of $\mM$ in this state (modular autonomy). We define the subsystem flow, which measures the departure from this error correction regime. Away from autonomy, the infinitesimal flow quantifies relative-entropy loss, while the history algebra and persistent core describe which observables the modular orbit generates and retains. We call an inclusion ergodic when modular orbits generate everything and retain nothing. Analytic continuation of subsystem flow yields Petz recovery maps and a family of positive inclusion parent Hamiltonians. We show that, in general, evolving with these parent Hamiltonians allows $\mN$ to leave $\mM$, and in some cases, it can generate the entire $\mM\vee\mM'$. Inclusions with a common cyclic and separating vector generate everything, and standard inclusions of factors, such as those of nested subregions in QFT, are ergodic. Moreover, the $L^2$-nuclearity property implies that the spectrum of parent Hamiltonians is discrete. We define a dissipative semigroup by repeating the Petz recovery map, whose fixed-point algebra is the modular persistent core and whose spectrum is gapped under the assumption of $L^2$-nuclearity. We conjecture that the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of inclusion parent Hamiltonians can be used to define local spectral measures of quantum chaos.
papers.summary: The paper develops a framework—subsystem flow—to quantify how a subalgebra (mathcal Nsubsetmathcal M) fails to be preserved under modular dynamics, linking this to quantum error correction, Petz recovery, and the emergence of parent Hamiltonians that can drive (mathcal N) to generate the full algebra. It proposes that the spectral data of these Hamiltonians could serve as local diagnostics of quantum chaos, offering a new algebraic perspective on operator dynamics in many‑body and quantum field systems.

papers.title: Exact Infrared Triangle in Gravity with Long-Range Interactions
papers.authors: Sangmin Choi, Ameya Kadhe, Prahar Mitra, Andrea Puhm
papers.abstract: Einstein gravity coupled to massless matter exhibits universality in the infrared. In the presence of long-range interactions we show that a novel superrotation charge conservation is equivalent to the massless limit of the classical logarithmic soft graviton theorem, and we propose a formula for the corresponding tail to the displacement memory. These results, which extend earlier work on gravity coupled to massive matter in a qualitatively different way, are exact in the gravitational coupling and reveal that long-range gravitational dressings resum. We also compute higher-order corrections to the known superrotation charge which are exact in the gravitational coupling and would correspond to a 1-loop exact correction to the Cachazo-Strominger subleading soft graviton theorem.
papers.summary: This work establishes an exact equivalence between a novel superrotation charge conservation law and the massless limit of the logarithmic soft graviton theorem in Einstein gravity with long-range interactions, providing a precise formula for the associated displacement memory tail. It also derives higher-order corrections to the superrotation charge that are exact in the gravitational coupling, corresponding to a 1-loop exact correction to the Cachazo–Strominger subleading soft graviton theorem.

papers.title: Magnetic-slope crossovers in the QCD bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio
papers.authors: Aalok Misra, Shivam S. Kushwah, Keshav Dasgupta, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon
papers.abstract: How a magnetic field alters dissipation in quark--gluon matter is almost unconstrained from first principles, since real-time transport is not directly accessible to lattice simulation. Using a top-down MQGP-inspired M/string-theory construction of a QCD-like thermal plasma, together with a kinetic-theory identity within a specified single-mode quasiparticle truncation and a compatibility construction using available lattice equation-of-state data, we propose a normalization-insensitive sign prediction that the field slope of the longitudinal bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio \zeta_\parallel/\eta_\parallel reverses sign twice with temperature---below and above the deconfinement pseudo-critical temperature T_0, at T_1<T_0<T_2 (the lower reversal T_1 conditional on a stated pion-gas rate inequality). A kinetic-theory identity with phase-appropriate carriers, a quark--gluon plasma above T_0 and a chiral pion gas below, reproduces the same pattern, and lattice speed-of-sound data can be shown to be consistent as well. The bottom-up VQCD in the deconfined phase supports a negative slope for large temperatures; the slope crossover is not resolvable from the available \zeta_\parallel/s, \eta_\parallel/s plots.
papers.summary: The paper studies how a magnetic field modifies the bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio in a QCD-like plasma, using a holographic MQGP-inspired M/string-theory construction combined with kinetic-theory identities and lattice data. It predicts a double sign reversal of the field slope of ζ_π/η_π across the deconfinement temperature, supported by both holographic and bottom-up VQCD analyses.

papers.title: Imaging the two-sided black hole interior with four-point correlators
papers.abstract: We propose a boundary four-point function smeared with wavepackets, which probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole. At high frequencies, boundary wavepackets aimed at an interior bulk point travel along geodesics and scatter locally about the bulk point, factorizing the correlator into a flat-space like scattering amplitude. To obtain this configuration, we utilize a non-trivial time ordering of operators, and also use one state-dependent operator insertion moved halfway across the thermal circle. An interesting property of this observable is that it also probes features of nontrivial states: null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon show up as jumps in the observed signal as the bulk point crosses them, thereby imaging the black hole interior.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a boundary four-point function, smeared with wavepackets, that probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole by factorizing into a flat-space scattering amplitude at high frequencies. It demonstrates that null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon produce observable jumps, effectively imaging the black hole interior via a non-trivial time ordering and a state-dependent operator insertion.

papers.title: Extension of Poincare superalgebra via hidden symmetries
papers.abstract: Isometries of a manifold and special types of spinors called Killing spinors which are related to Killing vector fields constitute a symmetry superalgebra structure corresponding to Poincare superalgebra. The antisymmetric generalization of Killing vector fields to higher degree forms which are called Killing-Yano forms are considered. The odd part of the Poincare superalgebra is extended from the space of Killing vector fields and their rotational representation to the space of special odd Killing-Yano forms and special even closed conformal Killing-Yano forms. The even part is again corresponds to the space of Killing spinors. By defining the relevant brackets, we show that hidden symmetries and Killing spinors together define an extension of the Poincare superalgebra.
papers.summary: The paper extends the Poincaré superalgebra by incorporating hidden symmetries encoded in Killing‑Yano forms and special closed conformal Killing‑Yano forms, thereby enlarging the odd part of the algebra. It demonstrates that these geometric structures, together with Killing spinors, furnish a consistent superalgebraic framework that generalizes the standard supersymmetry algebra.

papers.title: Self-Force and Bremsstrahlung in Finite Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study the self-force and the accompanying Bremsstrahlung for a moving point charge in nonlinear electrodynamics with finite self-field and self-energy. The self-force in the Maxwell theory has been the subject of many studies, often by renowned physicists. After reviewing Coleman's lucid treatise for Maxwell among them, we wish to explore the same question in the Born--Infeld theory, our prototype. We independently compute the local self-force and the global radiative dissipation, and show how the two are mutually consistent. Despite the nonlinearity turning off for the asymptotic radiative field, its residual effect survives via the effective multipole moments of a moving charge, allowing deviation from Maxwell. We close with a detailed discussion about two different manifestations of the self-force in the literature and how these enter our computation. One of the appendices explores Born--Infeld ModMax as a generalization.
papers.summary: The paper computes the local self‑force and global radiative loss for a point charge in Born–Infeld electrodynamics, showing consistency between the two and highlighting residual nonlinear effects via effective multipole moments. It also discusses how these results differ from Maxwell theory and touches on extensions to Born–Infeld ModMax.

papers.title: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
papers.authors: Shuntaro Aoki, Zhehan Qin, Masahide Yamaguchi, Yuhang Zhu
papers.abstract: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.
papers.summary: The paper establishes a general exclusion rule that guarantees the absence of oscillatory signals from a class of heavy-field exchanges in cosmological correlators, using spectral decomposition and field redefinitions to prove the result to all loop orders. It also provides the first explicit calculation of a nonvanishing triangle-loop signal in a toy model with chemical potentials, illustrating how such diagrams evade the exclusion rule.

papers.title: Anti-periodic Gravitino and Dirac Effective Operators
papers.abstract: Introducing a preserved $U(1)_R$ symmetry forbids gravitini Majorana masses while allowing a Dirac mass. We investigate how a Dirac mass for gravitini can be described by an effective operator in $N=1$ superspace, in analogy with the well-known Dirac gaugino mass. We find that the corresponding spin-$3/2$ bilinear operator can be expressed in terms of gauge-invariant gravitino curvature superfields coupled through a nonlocal kernel involving an inverse d'Alembertian. We study this construction in minimal five-dimensional supergravity compactified on $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$. The gravitino satisfies anti-periodic boundary conditions induced by a Scherk-Schwarz twist. The physical Kaluza-Klein Dirac masses then appear as poles in the two-point functions of the curvature superfields associated with sources localized at the endpoints. Separation of physical and gauge modes relates these propagators to a quadratic fermionic kernel represented by a $16\times16$ matrix. Its elements match the fermionic components of two invariants written in $N=1$ superspace, including their spinor contractions and normalization. This matching is carried out on a fixed background with a nonzero radion auxiliary field.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a gauge‑invariant superspace operator that generates a Dirac mass for the gravitino in five‑dimensional supergravity compactified on an orbifold, using a nonlocal kernel with an inverse d'Alembertian. It then matches the resulting Kaluza–Klein spectrum to a 16×16 fermionic kernel derived from two N=1 superspace invariants, illustrating how anti‑periodic boundary conditions from a Scherk–Schwarz twist produce physical Dirac masses.

papers.title: Holographic Wilsonian RG of Yang-Mills theory in AdS
papers.abstract: In this work, we extend the equilibrium-evolution duality between stochastic quantization and Wilsonian renormalization to non-abelian gauge theories in anti-de Sitter space, for which the radial coordinate of AdS plays the role of the stochastic time. We show, to all orders in the fields for bulk theories without explicit radial dependence, that the Langevin distribution at time $t$ is the product of the ultraviolet and infrared radial wavefunctions at the cutoff $\epsilon=t$. We therefore identify this Langevin process as the ground-state (Doob) transform of the radial evolution. By explicit calculation, we also extend the existing dictionary in the stochastic-renormalization duality: the radial component of the bulk field is Zwanziger's stochastic gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization; and the bulk gauge $A_z=\alpha^{-1}\partial_iA_i$ is Zwanziger's gauge. We also obtain the expressions for the triple-trace and quadruple-trace couplings of the holographic Wilsonian action at finite cutoff in closed form; in the infrared, they reduce to the known gluon correlators and, at the total-energy pole, to flat-space Yang-Mills amplitudes as expected. Although our explicit results are provided at tree-level and derived in AdS$_4$, we also comment on the de Sitter counterpart of these statements and on the loop corrections.
papers.summary: This paper extends the stochastic quantization–Wilsonian RG duality to non‑abelian gauge theories in AdS, showing that the radial coordinate acts as stochastic time and deriving closed‑form expressions for multi‑trace couplings at finite cutoff. The results reproduce known gluon correlators in the IR and flat‑space Yang‑Mills amplitudes at the energy pole, offering a new holographic Wilsonian framework for Yang‑Mills theory.

papers.title: Holographic Counterterms from Restricted Weyl Symmetry in Even-Dimensional Einstein-AdS Gravity
papers.abstract: We develop a symmetry-based approach to renormalization for even-dimensional Einstein-AdS gravity based on infinitesimal bulk Weyl transformations that preserve its field equations asymptotically. We determine a bulk-covariant completion of the Einstein-Hilbert density by requiring its variation under restricted Weyl transformations with parameter $\Sigma(X)$ to vanish modulo terms whose integrals remain finite as the radial cutoff is removed. This requirement induces two types of compensating terms with fixed couplings: the Euler density and a hierarchy of covariant total derivatives. The resulting recursive relations admit a factorized solution in terms of shifted Laplacians, yielding a closed-form completion in arbitrary even bulk dimensions. On Einstein backgrounds, these expressions agree, after matching normalizations, with those obtained through the ambient construction of conformal invariants. The associated renormalized-volume identity establishes on-shell finiteness for Euclidean AlAdS Einstein geometries in arbitrary even dimensions. The prescription reproduces the known conformally renormalized actions in four, six and eight dimensions and provides an explicit ten-dimensional completion involving powers of the Laplacian up to $\Box^3$. Applications to eight- and ten-dimensional AdS black holes with non-conformally-flat Einstein horizons yield finite on-shell actions in agreement with Holographic Renormalization.
papers.summary: This work constructs a bulk‑covariant completion of the Einstein‑Hilbert action in even‑dimensional AdS spacetimes by enforcing invariance under restricted Weyl transformations, yielding a closed‑form expression that automatically cancels divergences in the on‑shell action. The resulting counterterms reproduce known holographic renormalization results in 4, 6, 8 dimensions and extend them to ten dimensions, demonstrating finiteness for AdS black holes with non‑conformally‑flat horizons.

papers.title: Multiparticle residues of open-string tachyon amplitudes from DDF sewing
papers.abstract: We compute the maximal simultaneous residues of color-ordered tachyon disk amplitudes in the critical open bosonic string by summing all physical intermediate states. Sewing cubic Del Giudice--Di Vecchia--Fubini (DDF) vertices reduces this sum to Gaussian contractions for any planar cubic tree, with the internal levels specified independently. Each internal level fixes an exact finite mode cutoff. The residue then follows by coefficient extraction in the sewing variables from a determinant prefactor times the exponential of a quadratic form in the sources. With consistent sewing conventions, the local-coordinate scales cancel between the vertices and the sewing metric. At four points, cubic local maps and a one-boson stress-tensor Ward identity give an all-order resummation that recovers the Veneziano pole coefficients. The same construction gives explicit matrices for the five-point double residue and the six-point comb and snowflake, with low-level checks against independent Koba--Nielsen expansions. The determinant is the vacuum sewing factor of the transverse bosons. We formulate the operator, coordinate-map and measure identities needed to relate this construction to Grunsky operators and the full higher-point Koba--Nielsen top forms.
papers.summary: The paper develops a systematic method to compute maximal residues of color‑ordered open‑string tachyon disk amplitudes by sewing Del Giudice–Di Vecchia–Fubini (DDF) vertices, reducing the sum over intermediate states to Gaussian contractions on planar cubic trees. It demonstrates explicit results for four‑, five‑ and six‑point cases, reproducing Veneziano pole coefficients and providing determinant prefactors that match Koba–Nielsen expansions, thereby offering a new perspective on higher‑point string amplitude structures.

papers.title: Generalized Kosmann derivative and symmetry operators on Dirac structures
papers.abstract: We develop a spinorial symmetry framework for metric Dirac structures in $H$-twisted exact Courant algebroids. A generalized metric equips a Dirac structure with an intrinsic Riemannian Lie-algebroid geometry and identifies it isometrically with the positive subbundle of the generalized tangent bundle. For sections preserving the generalized metric, we prove an exact intertwining between the positive-spinor Kosmann--Dorfman action and the intrinsic Kosmann derivative. The comparison is independent of the auxiliary compatible generalized connection. Within the intrinsic geometry we derive Killing--Yano (KY) and conformal Killing--Yano (CKY) integrability identities, construct Killing-spinor-preserving operators from odd special KY and even special closed CKY forms, and obtain these forms from Hermitian bilinears of Killing spinors with imaginary Killing number. We illustrate the framework on a global Dirac structure over $S^2\times S^1$ with nontrivial $H$-flux class and rank-two anchor. Its spin connection and symmetry operators are explicit, and its Killing-spinor space is a transverse family $C^\infty(S^1,\mathbb C^2)$. Finally, intrinsic Killing sections act on Killing spinors by a Lie algebra representation. For a graph Dirac structure over $S^3$, the odd Jacobi identity of the Hermitian-current bracket fails by a phase, and adjoining a single even phase generator yields a Lie superalgebra. These results connect generalized isometries, hidden spinorial symmetries, and flux-sensitive Lie-algebroid geometry.
papers.summary: The paper develops a spinorial symmetry framework for Dirac structures in H‑twisted Courant algebroids, deriving Killing‑Yano and conformal Killing‑Yano integrability identities and constructing symmetry operators from special forms. It illustrates the formalism on explicit S^2×S^1 and S^3 examples, linking generalized isometries to flux‑dependent Lie‑algebroid geometry.

papers.title: Thermodynamics within and across AdS Gauss--Bonnet holographic CFTs
papers.abstract: We study thermal competition within individual holographic conformal field theories (CFTs) and across theories with different anomaly coefficients in five-dimensional AdS Gauss--Bonnet gravity. We derive the work term conjugate to the dimensionless coupling from the boundary first law and use a common boundary clock to compare charged spherical saddles at fixed external source. Varying this source drives a first-order switch between the CFTs at the endpoints of the chosen coupling interval. In the unit-lapse cylinder clock with the zero-type-D vacuum energy, strict concavity at fixed radius reduces the global comparison to these two endpoints. The preferred coupling jumps across the coexistence line, whose slope is related to the entropy difference by a generalized Clapeyron relation. Where the Einstein endpoint itself undergoes small--large coexistence, a third saddle joins the competition and produces a kink in the cross-theory boundary. A compensating change of the external control preserves saddle ordering under finite energy shifts. Within fixed CFTs, we determine the neutral Hawking--Page line and the charged small--large black hole coexistence surface. The critical charge tends to zero at a finite coupling. The entropy gap closes with exponent one half, and the heat capacity diverges with exponent two thirds along a temperature sweep at the critical charge.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes thermal phase transitions in five‑dimensional AdS Gauss–Bonnet holographic CFTs, deriving a work term conjugate to the Gauss–Bonnet coupling and mapping first‑order switches between distinct CFTs via a generalized Clapeyron relation. It also characterizes neutral Hawking–Page transitions and charged small–large black hole coexistence, finding critical exponents for entropy and heat capacity at the critical charge.

papers.title: Matching lattice and continuum chiral determinants at finite volume
papers.abstract: Recent formulations of lattice chiral gauge theories define a complex fermion weight either through Craig's gauge-invariant overlap measure or, following Hsu and Witten, through a continuum Weyl determinant on a reconstructed gauge connection, with its phase fixed by the five-dimensional $\eta$-invariant. For one $SU(5)$ generation on a flat four-torus, we prove that their relative weights agree in the continuum limit along smooth gapped paths, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang-Mills counterterm, whose coefficient we determine. On bounded smooth families a uniform Dirac gap suffices: the vacuum expansion need not converge. We obtain explicit uniform convergence rates for the logarithmic variations and, for Craig's interpolation, prove the reconstruction bounds that the matching requires, extending Hsu's small-field comparison to finite amplitude. For Hsu's reflection-positive reconstruction with flat collars, the phase variations still match, while the logarithmic coefficient of the quadratic counterterm is enhanced by a calculable, profile-dependent factor. In a hypercharge background on which the vacuum expansion diverges, numerical comparisons at the input gauge field support quadratic convergence of the phase, whereas the modulus acquires a logarithmic correction to quadratic scaling, whose coefficient follows analytically from the free overlap vacuum polarization.
papers.summary: The paper proves that Craig’s overlap measure and Hsu–Witten’s continuum Weyl determinant give the same chiral weight for a single SU(5) generation on a four‑torus, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang–Mills counterterm, and it supplies explicit convergence rates and reconstruction bounds for the phase and modulus in both smooth and hypercharge backgrounds.

papers.title: Accelerating solitons in Rindler space
papers.abstract: Relativistic nonlinear field theories that are integrable in two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime remain integrable in Rindler space. We investigate the properties of classical sine-Gordon (SG) solitons in Rindler space. Accelerating observers in each of the two Rindler wedges can see only a portion of the full soliton in Minkowski spacetime; this portion itself forms a soliton carrying a partial topological charge. The soliton solution admits the following interpretation: a soliton incoming from the horizon decelerates to stop at some point, then falls back and accelerates to the speed of light toward the horizon. Energy can flow into and out of the Rindler horizon. The higher energy soliton gains energy from the horizon while the lower one loses energy.
papers.summary: This paper shows that integrable relativistic field theories, such as the sine‑Gordon model, retain their integrability when formulated in Rindler coordinates. It studies how a soliton appears to an accelerating observer, revealing that only a portion of the soliton is visible, carrying a fractional topological charge, and that energy can flow across the Rindler horizon.

papers.title: Is Spin Slow in Hot QCD?
papers.abstract: Promoting spin to a hydrodynamic variable requires slow relaxation, as mass-suppressed helicity flips in hot QCD suggest. Using the full leading-order collision operator, we show instead that light-quark spin damps at the transport rate $g^4T\ln(1/g)$, nearly as fast as vector currents. Since spatial spin locks to momentum, helicity-conserving soft, small-angle scatterings readily rotate it. Damping involves multiple kinetic modes beyond a single relaxation time, global rotation adds only reversible precession, and stronger coupling further disfavors a slow spin mode in quark-gluon plasma.
papers.summary: This work shows that light‑quark spin in hot QCD does not behave as a slow hydrodynamic mode; instead, it damps at the same transport rate as vector currents, (g^4Tln(1/g)), due to efficient helicity‑conserving scatterings. The study highlights that multiple kinetic modes, rather than a single relaxation time, govern spin dynamics, and that global rotation only induces reversible precession.

papers.title: Discrete anomaly inflow from SymTFT of $U(1)$ global symmetry: the modified Villain resolution
papers.abstract: We construct a lattice SymTFT for a $U(1)$ global symmetry with anomaly coefficient $k$ using the modified Villain formulation, in which the spin structure required for odd $k$ is realised explicitly by lattice Majorana fermions. We demonstrate that the same Majorana fermions sit at the junctions of the symmetry lines, exactly where the fusion of two $U(1)$ elements wraps around the circle. From the lattice algebra of lines and junctions we derive the $R$- and $F$-symbols in the bulk and on the gapped boundary, and show that for odd $k$ the boundary $F$-symbol obeys the Gu-Wen relation for the $U(1)$ symmetry defect, without passing through a bosonic shadow.
