Restricting to $\mathbb{Z}_2\subset U(1)$, we reproduce the mod-4 anomalous phase from a mapping torus and the fermionic stacking rule. As a simple application of this SymTFT, we also determine which subgroups $\mathbb{Z}_d\subset U(1)$ can be gauged and the symmetry of the resulting theories. This is a first step towards deriving, from the anomaly inflow of a continuous symmetry, the junction data of global anomalies beyond group cohomology.
papers.summary: This work builds a lattice SymTFT for a U(1) global symmetry with anomaly coefficient k using a modified Villain construction, explicitly realizing the required spin structure for odd k via lattice Majorana fermions. It derives bulk and boundary fusion data, reproduces known Z2 anomalies, and identifies which U(1) subgroups can be gauged, offering a step toward extracting junction data for continuous symmetry anomalies beyond group cohomology.

papers.title: Finite cyclic monodromy in BMS3 gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate inducing data for three dimensional asymptotically flat BMS gravity on hyperbolic Virasoro orbits with winding, which contain no constant supermomentum, and the restriction of formal smooth equivariant sections to global Lorentz orbits. Using the developing map of the associated Hill operator we rederive their stabilizer and show that, in the spin double cover, it is the direct product of a line with a cyclic group of even order. The character of the cyclic factor is therefore a discrete inducing label independent of the continuous one, unlike for the massive BMS particles, where it is fixed by the spin. At points with the corresponding finite rotational symmetry, restriction of formal smooth equivariant sections to a global Lorentz orbit yields the finite cyclic equivariance condition, while an independently defined unitary global branch realizes the associated finite difference equation. At points with timelike projected momentum we derive the resulting ladder of Poincare helicities, show that the projected rest energy is not an orbit invariant, construct locally flat winding BMS geometries with hyperbolic Lorentz holonomy, prove that the smooth real periodic near horizon current model excludes these winding orbits, and obtain selection rules and closed form expressions for finite monodromy resolved orbital functionals. A unitary realization on the full infinite dimensional orbit is not constructed, and the interpretation of the cyclic sectors in quantum gravity remains conjectural.
papers.summary: The paper studies the structure of BMS3 asymptotically flat spacetimes by analysing hyperbolic Virasoro orbits with nontrivial winding, revealing that the stabiliser is a product of a line and a finite cyclic group whose character is an independent discrete label. These results suggest new sectors in flat‑space holography and may inform the construction of celestial amplitudes, though a full quantum realization remains open.

papers.title: Gauge Theory Bootstrap with varying $N_c$
papers.authors: Rafael Cordoba, Yifei He, Martin Kruczenski, Derek Ping, Jignesh Mohanty, Emil Alegria
papers.abstract: We use the Gauge Theory Bootstrap to study asymptotically free gauge theories with a varying number of colors $N_c$. The parameter $N_c$ enters the computation through the sum rules and asymptotic form factors, allowing us to tune this microscopic parameter directly and examine the corresponding low-energy strongly coupled dynamics. For $3\le N_c\le 12$, we extract the scattering lengths, effective ranges, and low-energy constants $\bar{l}_i$, and study their $N_c$ dependence. We also obtain the $\sigma$, $\rho$, and $f_2$ resonances for the same range of $N_c$. The $\rho$ and $f_2$ masses depend only weakly on $N_c$, and their widths decrease as $N_c$ increases, consistent with the $1/N_c$ scaling expected for conventional $q\bar{q}$ mesons. In contrast, the $\sigma$ meson mass and width both increase with $N_c$, in agreement with a previous unitarized $\chi$PT analysis. These results provide a further test of the Gauge Theory Bootstrap for studying asymptotically free gauge theories.
papers.summary: The paper applies the Gauge Theory Bootstrap to study how scattering observables and resonance properties vary with the number of colors (N_c) in asymptotically free gauge theories, finding that (ho) and (f_2) masses are almost (N_c)-independent while their widths shrink as (1/N_c), whereas the (sigma) meson’s mass and width grow with (N_c). These results test the bootstrap’s ability to capture nonperturbative dynamics across a range of gauge group sizes.

papers.title: Holographic viscous transport in scalar-coupled Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.authors: Tao Ma, Song He, Li Li
papers.abstract: We test horizon formulas for the shear and bulk viscosities of a holographic plasma against viscosities extracted directly from retarded stress-tensor correlators. We work in a five-dimensional Einstein-dilaton-Gauss-Bonnet model calibrated to the lattice QCD equation of state at zero baryon density. UV-finite renormalized correlators are obtained by including the required curvature and scalar counterterms, and the fluctuation equations are solved while retaining the full dependence on the Gauss-Bonnet coupling $\alpha$, without using a horizon conservation law or an entropy-production formula. For constant coupling, the horizon conserved-current calculation reproduces the boundary Kubo results in both channels. For the scalar-dependent coupling studied here, both methods find a minimum in the shear-viscosity-to-entropy-density ratio $\eta/s$. In the bulk channel, the conserved-current calculation truncated at first order in $\alpha$ yields a lower peak height in $\zeta/s$, with the peak temperature nearly unchanged relative to the boundary result. For both couplings, the unmodified Eling-Oz (EO) formula, $\zeta/s=(4\pi)^{-1}(\partial\phi_h/\partial\ln s)^2$, reproduces the boundary result for $\zeta/s$, where $\phi_h$ is the horizon value of the scalar. The prefactor $1/(4\pi)$ is thus retained even when the Gauss-Bonnet interaction shifts $\eta/s$ from this value. These results provide a direct boundary benchmark for horizon prescriptions and support the unmodified EO formula beyond constant coupling.
papers.summary: The study tests horizon-based formulas for shear and bulk viscosities in a five-dimensional Einstein-dilaton-Gauss-Bonnet model calibrated to lattice QCD, confirming that the Eling-Oz formula remains valid even with a scalar-dependent Gauss-Bonnet coupling. It demonstrates that both horizon-conserved current and Kubo methods yield consistent results, revealing a minimum in η/s and a peak in ζ/s that are largely unaffected by the coupling’s magnitude.

papers.title: Infinite spin superparticles
papers.abstract: We obtain infinite spin representations of the super-Poincar\'e algebra from a higher-derivative superparticle action on a super-Minkowski background in 3, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions. Super-twistor transforms are performed, and used to deduce first-quantised spectra.
papers.summary: This paper constructs infinite‑spin representations of the super‑Poincaré algebra in 3, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions by analyzing a higher‑derivative superparticle action on super‑Minkowski space. Using super‑twistor transforms, the authors extract the first‑quantised spectra, linking higher‑spin supermultiplets to twistor‑based formulations.

papers.title: De Sitter Gravity and Emergent Time from Fusion Matrix Product States and SYK
papers.abstract: We propose a quantum-mechanical model dual to two-dimensional de Sitter (dS) gravity. It is a quantum channel, defined by a matrix product state that fuses one spin at each step, and is related to a limit of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model without chord crossings. Its simplest part is a random walk with an emergent $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry, which we identify with the symmetry of the future boundary of dS. It selects a time variable in which the walk obeys the Schwarzian action and yields the disk amplitude of dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. As the simplest case, we consider free massless scalar fields in the fixed background of dS$_2$. We find the agreement of the two-point function in the Bunch-Davies vacuum and the matching of symmetry. Our construction provides a concrete model for the dS/CFT correspondence for two-dimensional de Sitter gravity.
papers.summary: The authors construct a quantum channel defined by a matrix product state that models 2D de Sitter gravity, showing that its emergent SL(2,ℝ) symmetry reproduces the Bunch‑Davies two‑point function and the disk amplitude of dS JT gravity. This provides a concrete dS/CFT duality framework using a SYK‑like random walk that yields the Schwarzian action.

papers.title: Covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus, non-dissipative transport and the chiral anomaly in inhomogeneous systems with nontrivial momentum-space topology
papers.abstract: We review, systematize and extend the covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus for fermions in non-Abelian gauge fields and its applications to systems inhomogeneous in coordinate space with nontrivial momentum-space topology: the non-Abelian chiral separation and quantum Hall effects, their stability under interactions, the Fermi-surface invariant of inhomogeneous systems and the non-elliptic models that carry it, with their equilibrium chiral magnetic effect, the factorization of the chiral anomaly into the instanton number and the momentum-space invariant $N_3$, and the noncommutative-geometric form of the invariants. Previous results are brought to common conventions, with hypotheses stated and notions defined. New results: the characterization of the operators whose covariant symbol is gauge-field independent and the ordering independence of the integrated anomaly; the anomaly factorization on a closed four-manifold without the homotopy hypothesis, the factorization into instanton number and $N_3$ holding exactly when the untwisted index vanishes; the Luttinger--Ward identity behind the renormalized-velocity current and the continuum conditions replacing the compactness of the Brillouin zone in the non-renormalization theorems; the identification of the Moyal $N_3$ of the chiral separation effect with the fibre degree of the principal symbol; the residue evaluation of the Fermi-surface invariant of the non-elliptic models, in the continuum and on a lattice, and the equilibrium current of the conserved charge along the magnetic field that it implies -- a chiral magnetic effect permitted by the non-Hamiltonian form of these models -- which the model with spherical Fermi surfaces trades for a chiral separation effect and a single-Weyl anomaly, and a modification of it restores at the price of the anomaly; and the index-pairing form of the chiral separation invariant.
papers.summary: This paper extends the covariant Wigner–Weyl formalism to fermions in non‑Abelian gauge backgrounds, deriving new expressions for the chiral anomaly that factor into instanton number and a momentum‑space invariant N3. It also introduces a Luttinger–Ward identity for the renormalized‑velocity current and characterizes non‑elliptic models that support equilibrium chiral magnetic effects without a compact Brillouin zone.

papers.title: Love numbers for the Myers-Perry geometry
papers.abstract: We analyze Love numbers for scalar fields in the Myers-Perry geometry in arbitrary dimensions. The tidal responses of black holes are specified by two constants which encode a potential logarithmic running and the Love number. We argue that the parameter specifying the running is not sensitive to the structure of the horizon, and we explicitly compute this parameter for Myers-Perry black holes in arbitrary dimensions by utilizing the asymptotic expansion of the wave equation. The Love numbers rely on the details of the boundary conditions at the horizon, and we compute them using several distinct approximations.
papers.summary: The paper computes the tidal Love numbers for scalar perturbations of Myers‑Perry black holes in arbitrary dimensions, deriving both the logarithmic running parameter and the horizon‑dependent Love numbers via asymptotic analysis of the wave equation. It explores how different horizon boundary conditions affect the tidal response, providing analytic approximations for the multipole coefficients.

papers.title: Twisting IKKT with branes
papers.abstract: Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. Beyond the two twists available at any finite $N$, which we studied in our previous work, we find five additional classes at infinite rank which require non-commuting backgrounds associated with D-branes in IIB supergravity. Together, these twists realize representatives of every equivalence class of twisting supercharges in flat-space type IIB supergravity recently classified by the first author; however, the precise form of the orbit stratification differs. This difference is related to a higher central extension of the IIB superalgebra that appears in our treatment of the IKKT model in the BV formalism. Expanding around the non-commutative backgrounds gives worldvolume theories on products of A- and B-branes, including four-dimensional BF theory on an emergent D3-brane. We relate all these twists to deformations of BCOV theory (the closed string field theory of the topological B-model) using the open-closed duality of classical string field theory. For one of the twists with Spin$(7)$ symmetry, we also show the localization of the IKKT partition function by Moore, Nekrasov, and Shatashvili can be directly reconstructed with the BV formalism, with their auxiliary field completion encoded by quadratic antifield terms. Throughout, we provide self-contained treatments of the formal techniques we employ.
papers.summary: This work classifies all supersymmetric twists of the IKKT matrix model, uncovering five new infinite‑rank twists that involve non‑commutative D‑brane backgrounds and realize every flat‑space type IIB supercharge orbit. The authors then show how these twists give rise to worldvolume theories—including BF theory on an emergent D3‑brane—and relate them to deformations of BCOV theory via open‑closed duality, providing a BV‑formalism derivation of the IKKT partition‑function localization.

papers.title: A precision bound for gravitational transseries
papers.abstract: We propose that the large $N$ transseries of a holographic observable above the black hole threshold admits a precision bound, a limit on how precisely the transseries can determine the observable at finite $N$, set by the data of its D-brane instanton sectors. In doing so, we develop methods in large $N$ resurgence, based on the work of \'{E}calle, that capture the $e^{-N^2}$ asymptotics of gravitational saddles beyond the $e^{-N}$ instantons. Under an assumption on the growth of the D-brane instanton sums that we expect in the black hole phase, we find an analytic obstruction to the resummation of the large $N$ transseries. This obstruction sets the precision bound. As our main example and consistency check, we study the $\frac{1}{16}$-BPS index of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills and its black hole. We derive relations between the D-brane instanton data on thermal AdS and on the black hole, in the form of a duality that exchanges the numbers of D-brane instantons on the two backgrounds. In the index, these relations reproduce the actions of D3-branes wrapped on the black hole. We conclude with our expectations for generic situations and their relation to the double-cone wormhole.
papers.summary: We show that the large‑N transseries of a holographic observable above the black‑hole threshold is bounded in precision by its D‑brane instanton data, revealing an analytic obstruction to full resummation and a duality between instanton sectors on thermal AdS and the black hole. This is illustrated for the 1/16‑BPS index of N=4 SYM, where the bound reproduces D3‑brane actions on the black‑hole geometry.

papers.title: The $(5,5)$ String
papers.abstract: We study an $N=(2,1)$ heterotic string with right-movers on $\mathbb R^{2,2}$ and left-movers of signature $(5,5)$, obtained by adjoining the lattice $\mathrm{II}_{3,3}$. Unlike the standard $N=(2,1)$ strings it requires no null current, and its target space remains four-dimensional. All of its states, an infinite tower with sixteen supercharges, are massless. For the neutral bosons, the Kutasov-Martinec determinant action is dual to a cubic action for a self-dual metric coupled to self-dual Maxwell fields, and we complete it with fermions using a single superfield. For the charged states we give evidence that the couplings are the structure constants of a Lie superalgebra formed by the physical states of the left-movers. We are thus led to propose that the classical target theory is a self-dual gauge theory for this superalgebra: every state of the string is a gauge field, and gravity is part of the gauge algebra. This would be a purely cubic field theory of all the modes of a closed string.
papers.summary: This paper constructs an N=(2,1) heterotic string with left‑movers on a (5,5) lattice, yielding an infinite tower of massless states with sixteen supercharges. It proposes that the target theory is a purely cubic self‑dual gauge theory whose gauge algebra includes gravity, suggesting a novel closed‑string field theory framework.

papers.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
papers.abstract: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes. Lastly, we provide a simple representation-theoretic argument regarding the recently proposed excited bound states of the model.
papers.summary: This paper numerically solves the SU(2) BFSS matrix model to obtain the ground state corresponding to a bound state of two D0-branes, reproducing the three-graviton coupling with high precision. It also demonstrates supersymmetric protection of the coupling and discusses possible excited bound states via representation theory.

papers.title: Decoupling Dynamics: A Tale of Two Limits
papers.abstract: The symmetries of a $d$-dimensional QFT are known to be captured by a topological theory in one dimension higher, the Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which is invariant under gauging finite symmetries of the QFT, but not under dynamical gauging of continuous symmetries. We show that the distinct SymTFTs of a $d$-dimensional QFT before and after dynamical gauging of a continuous Abelian symmetry arise as different topological limits of the same dynamical holographic gauge theory in $(d+1)$-dimensions. Gauging changes the boundary condition of this dynamical theory and thereby selects a different topological limit, explaining why the associated SymTFT changes. We give a fully quantum definition of these SymTFTs at the level of Hilbert spaces and operators by combining suitable limits of the bulk holographic theory with photon truncation. This construction clarifies how topological symmetry defects, charges, and anomalies survive while the dynamical information carried by currents is discarded. We study non-anomalous and anomalous examples, providing a complete quantum analysis for $(2+1)$-dimensional bulks. For a four-dimensional boundary theory with a mixed axial-vector anomaly, we recover the SymTFT of the non-invertible chiral symmetry that remains after gauging the vector symmetry.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT) of a d‑dimensional QFT before and after gauging a continuous Abelian symmetry can be obtained as distinct topological limits of a single dynamical holographic gauge theory in (d+1) dimensions, with the gauging changing the bulk boundary condition. By combining bulk limits with photon truncation, the authors give a fully quantum definition of SymTFTs, illustrating how topological defects, charges, and anomalies survive while dynamical current data is discarded, and they apply this to both non‑anomalous and anomalous examples, including a 4d theory with a mixed axial‑vector anomaly.

papers.title: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
papers.authors: Runze Chi, Meng Zeng, Tao Xiang, Yi-Zhuang You, Bertrand I. Halperin, Juven Wang
papers.abstract: Quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall systems is a bulk topological property, typically manifesting on gapless boundaries as spectral flow through chiral edge modes upon flux insertion. When the boundary is anomaly-free, it can be symmetrically gapped by symmetric mass generation (SMG) interactions. However, the effects on quantized charge pumping at an interacting gapped boundary are unclear. We address this using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder quasi-(2+1)d realization of the (1+1)d 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral fermion model with six-fermion interactions at one edge. We find gapless modes near the interacting edge for both weak and strong couplings, but the edge can be in a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling. We also identify spontaneous breaking of the model's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry above a critical interaction strength. Across all three boundary phases, we find quantized charge pumping with the same pumped charge per flux quantum. The spatial distribution of the pumped charge varies between phases. Besides charge pumping, we study how a single injected fermion propagates under open boundary conditions. In the SMG phase, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current develops at the endpoints of the gapped edge, which is absent in the weak- and strong-coupling limits. This current reveals a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to the SMG phase. Additionally, we propose an analogy between charge pumping in this model and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the (3+1)d Standard Model. The anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetries of the 3-4-5-0 model play a role analogous to the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry of the Standard Model. In both settings, charge pumping can be associated with a continuous deformation along a classically defined but quantum-anomalous direction, while a discrete subgroup remains an exact quantum symmetry.
papers.summary: This study uses DMRG to investigate charge pumping in a four-leg ladder realization of the 3-4-5-0 chiral fermion model, finding that the pumped charge per flux quantum remains quantized across weak, intermediate (SMG), and strong coupling regimes, though the spatial distribution of the pumped charge changes. The work also uncovers an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current at the endpoints of the gapped edge in the SMG phase and draws an analogy between this charge pumping and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the Standard Model.

papers.title: Dynamical entropy on local causal horizons: the Einstein equation of state and canonical-energy flux
papers.abstract: For a twist-free null hypersurface, the Hollands-Wald-Zhang (HWZ) representative $S_{\rm loc}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1-V\theta)dA$, local on each cross-section (cut), obeys an exact off-shell Raychaudhuri identity with no term linear in the expansion, so no final equilibrium cut is needed. Given an entropy density $1/4G$, the Unruh temperature $\kappa/2\pi$ of an approximate local boost, local equilibrium cuts, and stress-tensor conservation, equating the leading equilibrium change of $S_{\rm loc}$ to matter boost heat yields $R_{kk}=8\pi GT_{kk}$ for every null direction, hence the Einstein equation with undetermined cosmological constant, an equation of state in Jacobson's conditional sense. On a fixed caustic-free generator bundle with $dA=J\,dA_{\rm ref}$, the functional $S_{\rm L}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1+\ln J-V\theta)dA_{\rm ref}$ obeys an exact balance per reference cell with curvature, shear, and expansion terms all positive, so under null convergence $S_{\rm L}$ is nondecreasing for $V\geq0$ until the first caustic. Conversely, requiring this balance for positive affine parameter on every small bundle and null direction is equivalent to the Einstein equation, given conservation and the stated normalization. Cut-locality, positivity, and first-order HWZ normalization select the density $1+\ln J-V\theta$ uniquely within a two-function class. Both functionals depend on the affine origin; we give their shift laws, identify the anchoring-invariant content, and show the origin is physical data fixed by the equilibrium cut. Near equilibrium, $S_{\rm L}$ agrees with the HWZ dynamical entropy at first order, and the temperature-weighted change of its Hessian equals the HWZ modified canonical-energy flux for stationary-vacuum perturbations. At finite amplitude, $S_{\rm L}$ is only a monotone geometric functional; reading it as entropy requires a coarse-graining postulate, stated but not derived.
papers.summary: This work introduces a local entropy functional on null hypersurfaces that satisfies an exact off‑shell Raychaudhuri identity, allowing the Einstein equation to be derived as an equation of state without requiring a final equilibrium cut. It further defines a monotonic entropy‑like functional on fixed generator bundles, whose balance condition is equivalent to the null convergence condition and the Einstein equation, providing a new perspective on gravitational dynamics.

papers.title: Quivers with potential for quantum affine superalgebras
papers.abstract: We construct a surjective algebra homomorphism from the $K$-theoretic Hall algebras of certain quivers with potential to the (half) quantum affine and toroidal orthosymplectic superalgebras.
papers.summary: This paper builds a bridge between the algebraic structures of K‑theoretic Hall algebras for quivers with potential and the representation theory of quantum affine and toroidal orthosymplectic superalgebras, offering new tools for studying supersymmetric gauge theories and integrable systems. It provides explicit surjective homomorphisms that could be useful for constructing and analyzing supersymmetric partition functions and correlation functions in higher‑dimensional quantum field theories.

papers.title: A Positive Turn: Coupled Quintessence and Cosmological Neutrino Masses
papers.authors: Tian-Nuo Li, William Giar\`e, Guo-Hong Du, Eleonora Di Valentino, Luis A. Anchordoqui, Shao-Jiang Wang, Xin Zhang, Rong-Gen Cai
papers.abstract: In $\Lambda$CDM, the CMB and DESI BAO upper limits on the total neutrino mass are in tension with the lower bounds from oscillation experiments, and analyses allowing negative effective masses favor negative values. We investigate whether a coupled quintessence (CQ) model in which dark matter interacts with a canonical scalar field $\phi$ through an exponential mass coupling $m_{\rm c}(\phi)\propto e^{-\beta\phi/M_{\rm Pl}}$ can alleviate this tension. Combining CMB, DESI, and supernova data, we find that CQ yields neutrino-mass constraints comparable to those obtained in CPL and consistent with oscillation experiments within $2\sigma$ for normal ordering, without requiring the scalar-field equation of state to cross the phantom divide. We further show that it alleviates the tension more effectively than alternative interacting dark energy models that instead favor more negative effective masses. This comparison shows that whether dark sector interactions can relax neutrino mass bounds ultimately depends on the interplay of their effects on primary CMB anisotropies, geometry, growth, and lensing.
papers.summary: This study explores a coupled quintessence model where dark matter interacts with a scalar field, showing that neutrino mass bounds from CMB, BAO, and supernova data can be reconciled with oscillation experiments without invoking phantom dark energy. The analysis demonstrates that such dark‑sector interactions can alleviate the neutrino‑mass tension more effectively than other interacting dark‑energy scenarios by affecting CMB anisotropies, geometry, growth, and lensing.

papers.title: Cosmological Magnetic Fluctuations: Positivity Bounds and QCD Contributions
papers.abstract: We study thermal cosmological magnetic fluctuations in two complementary ways. First, we bound the equilibrium magnetic power spectrum in terms of two spectral moments. The proof uses the fluctuation--dissipation relation, spectral positivity, and the convexity and concavity of the thermal kernels. The bounds do not require a model for the spectral shape. They also apply to individual current contributions, using their own moments, and a known frequency threshold strengthens the upper bound. Second, we calculate a hadronic QCD contribution to cosmological magnetic fluctuations at leading electromagnetic order. We estimate the \(\rho\)-resonance contribution, which dominates the timelike hadronic contribution in our comparison. Examples from QCD, an electron--positron plasma and a cold collisional plasma test the bounds. The spectra describe fluctuations at the chosen cosmological epoch.
papers.summary: This paper derives model-independent bounds on the equilibrium magnetic power spectrum in a thermal cosmological setting using fluctuation–dissipation and spectral positivity, and then computes the leading QCD hadronic contribution, dominated by the ρ‑resonance, to these fluctuations. The authors test their bounds against QCD, electron–positron, and cold plasma examples, illustrating how the spectra evolve at different cosmological epochs.

papers.title: Critical schemes, jet syzygies, and twisted periods
papers.abstract: We study nonreduced critical schemes with prescribed support on nilpotent orbit closures and on the Kleinian singularity $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, and show that one specified minimal invariant syzygy among the first jet equations fixes their scheme structure. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N$ or $\mathfrak{so}_{2N}$ with Coxeter number $h$ and $p\ge2$ coprime to $h$, the selected polynomial is the coefficient of $s^{p+1}$ in $\det(1-sM)^{p/h}$, with reduced critical locus $\{M^p=0\}$, and the selecting syzygy is equivalent to the twisted period equation of Dubrovin and Feigin-Silantyev. The minimal invariant syzygies of that degree correspond to the lowest nonquadratic twisted periods, which, for $\mathfrak{so}_8$, form the standard representation of triality; in type D the Betti number alone does not determine the scheme. On $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, the selected polynomial is given by a terminating hypergeometric series. Restriction to Slodowy slices commutes with forming critical schemes and their nilradicals. These results determine, uniformly in rank and degree, the rings and nilradical filtrations through which the Schur and Macdonald indices of the corresponding Argyres-Douglas theories are proposed to arise as Hilbert series of arc spaces.
papers.summary: This paper studies the algebraic structure of critical schemes associated to nilpotent orbits and Kleinian singularities, showing that a single invariant syzygy determines their scheme structure. The results provide explicit descriptions of the rings and nilradical filtrations that underlie the Schur and Macdonald indices of Argyres-Douglas theories, offering a new algebraic perspective on these SCFT invariants.

papers.title: Earth-sized tests of long-range neutrino interactions
papers.abstract: Neutrinos may experience a new long-range force that distinguishes their flavors, mediated by an ultralight neutral boson of a new $U(1)'$ gauge symmetry and sourced by the electrons and nucleons of ordinary matter. Atmospheric neutrinos that cross the Earth would then feel a flavor-dependent potential that alters their oscillations. When the range of the force is about one Earth radius or less, this potential varies from point to point along each neutrino's path, since it comes mostly from the matter near the neutrino. Earlier limits approximated it, either as constant along the path or as following the local density of matter. We compute it exactly at every point of each path, for the Earth model of the IceCube analysis and over the distribution of heights at which the neutrinos are produced, and use it to analyze the 8-yr public IceCube DeepCore sample with the systematic uncertainties of that analysis. For mediator masses from $10^{-15}$ to $10^{-9}$ eV, where the Earth alone sources the potential, we set upper limits at 90% confidence level on the coupling of eight of 14 $U(1)'$ symmetries, those whose potential differs between $\nu_\mu$ and $\nu_\tau$. A potential held at its value at the detector would weaken our limits by factors of about 1-3. Below about $10^{-11}$-$10^{-10}$ eV, depending on the symmetry, our limits are stronger than those from tests of the equivalence principle.
papers.summary: This study examines how a new long-range flavor-dependent force mediated by an ultralight gauge boson would affect atmospheric neutrino oscillations as they traverse the Earth, computing the spatially varying potential for realistic Earth density profiles and IceCube production heights. Using eight years of IceCube DeepCore data, the authors set 90% CL upper limits on the coupling of several U(1)' symmetries, improving on equivalence principle bounds for mediator masses below ~10^-10 eV.

papers.title: Gravitational observables from a post-Carrollian expansion
papers.abstract: Einstein gravity, with a few exceptions, only admits nonlocal observables. This feature is often attributed to diffeomorphism invariance, since a gravitational field can thereby locally be transformed away. We show this attribution to be incorrect by constructing infinitely many exact ultralocal Dirac observables in (velocity dominated aka electric) Carroll gravity. The latter describes Einstein gravity's ultrarelativistic limit, is fully diffeomorphism invariant, and of independent interest in a variety of contexts. Starting from these Carroll observables a systematic construction of Dirac observables for Einstein gravity is outlined. The resulting "post-Carrollian" expansion is organized by the number of spatial gradients or fractional inverse powers of Newton's constant, where each partial sum is local.
papers.summary: The authors construct infinitely many exact ultralocal Dirac observables in Carroll gravity, the ultrarelativistic limit of Einstein gravity, and then outline a systematic post‑Carrollian expansion that yields local partial sums of Dirac observables for full Einstein gravity. This framework provides a new, gradient‑ordered approach to defining gauge‑invariant gravitational observables that could be useful for holographic and scattering‑amplitude applications.

papers.title: Ernst-Potential Driven Recovery of Kerr with Neural Networks
papers.authors: Veselin G. Filev, Stoytcho S. Yazadjiev
papers.abstract: We use artificial neural networks to recover the Kerr solution by directly minimizing a regularized Ernst sigma-model action. Reduction along the axial Killing direction avoids the divergence at the ergosphere. Compactified coordinates cover the entire black-hole exterior, while the network parametrization enforces the asymptotic data and axis regularity. For dimensionless spins $0.1 \le a/M \le 0.99$, the median maximum relative error in the recovered metric component $g_{\phi\phi}$ remains below $7.2\times10^{-4}$. When only the horizon rod length and angular momentum are prescribed, the networks also predict the mass with median relative errors below $1.8\times10^{-3}$. These results demonstrate the practicality of direct variational training for rotating black-hole geometries.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that a neural network can be trained to minimize a regularized Ernst sigma-model action and recover the Kerr metric with high precision across a wide spin range. The approach uses compactified coordinates and enforces asymptotic and axis regularity, achieving sub‑per‑mille errors in key metric components.

papers.title: Correlation Geometry and Emergent Space-Time from Stochastic Correlation Flows
papers.abstract: We propose an effective framework relating correlation geometry to stochastic flows of correlation projectors. Physical configurations are encoded by measures on spaces of self-adjoint operators, with physical equivalence defined by unitary conjugation. Assuming a smooth, spectrally separated correlation sector, local orthonormal frames define a Wilczek--Zee connection, while a Stratonovich gradient-flow ansatz preserves the projector constraints. In a local continuum approximation with massive fast modes, standard one-loop methods generate Yang--Mills-type terms and curvature terms of Einstein--Hilbert form. Along a smooth closed path, the trace of a cyclic product of projectors converges to the trace of the parallel-transport operator as the discretization is refined. We examine possible geometric, disordered, and topological regimes and motivate the stochastic dynamics through an effective open-system description. The first-order frame action defines a symplectic structure on the projector sector, providing a starting point for its relation to gravitational canonical variables. We identify the matching conditions required for an Ashtekar phase-space description and the assumptions connecting correlation geometry to induced interactions and emergent spacetime.
papers.summary: The paper develops a stochastic framework for correlation projectors that yields Yang–Mills and Einstein–Hilbert terms in a continuum limit, suggesting a route to emergent spacetime from operator measures. It connects Wilczek–Zee connections, Ashtekar phase space, and symplectic structures to open‑system dynamics, offering a potential bridge between gauge theory and gravity.

papers.title: Making Poisson {\sigma} again - an \'etude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
papers.abstract: The Poisson $\sigma$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $\Sigma$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = \Sigma \times G \to \Sigma$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,\omega)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,\Pi)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = \Sigma \times M \to \Sigma$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $\Sigma$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,\Pi)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $\omega$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.
papers.summary: This paper reformulates the Poisson sigma model as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle, interpreting its flat directions as linearizations of automorphisms of the bundle and analyzing the gauge anomaly in terms of gerbes. It then extends the construction to arbitrary principaloid bundles, providing a gerbe-based descent mechanism and a defect formulation that ensures global consistency via G‑equivariant structures.

papers.title: A consistent formulation of stochastic inflation II: Reassessing its role in nonlinear cosmological perturbations
papers.abstract: We question whether the conventional formulation of stochastic inflation can provide a quantitatively reliable description of cosmological perturbations. More fundamentally, we reassess the role and motivations of the stochastic approach to study cosmological perturbations, distinct from its well-founded motivation for resumming IR secular divergences. To provide a quantitative basis for this reassessment, we extend stochastic inflation beyond the linear regime by incorporating non-Markovian effects arising from infrared-ultraviolet interactions and terms quadratic in ultraviolet fluctuations, which generate non-white noise. We derive three-point correlation functions for a spectator scalar field in de Sitter space and a slow-roll inflaton including metric perturbations, demonstrating exact agreement with in-in quantum-field-theoretic predictions for superhorizon nonlinear evolution. Our results show that both non-Markovian effects and quadratic (higher order) noise terms are essential for quantitative accuracy, implying that the conventional stochastic-inflation framework is, at best, quantitatively justified only at linear order.
papers.summary: The authors extend stochastic inflation to include non‑Markovian and quadratic noise terms, deriving three‑point functions that match in‑in QFT results for spectator and inflaton fields in de Sitter/slow‑roll backgrounds. Their work demonstrates that conventional stochastic inflation is quantitatively reliable only at linear order, highlighting the necessity of higher‑order corrections for accurate superhorizon evolution.

papers.title: Maximally Chiral Eigenstate from Inverse Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
papers.abstract: We show that an ordered quantum state can support waves with a finite speed in one direction and exponentially small energies in the other. We prescribe this spectrum for a spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg eigenstate and reconstruct a nonlocal Hamiltonian. The thermodynamic construction selects the ordered, current-carrying state as a ground state. Its magnetic moment remains finite while its response to a weak field has a divergent slope. The entropy per spin vanishes only inversely with a logarithm of temperature, with an exact coefficient containing the golden ratio. Our spin-response calculations reveal a bound pair whose energy can be tuned without changing its intensity. Added exchange and smoother mode selection restore quadratic excitations at the lowest energies. These results connect the design of interactions to directional dynamics and unusual thermodynamics. We propose momentum-resolved spin spectroscopy, weak-field magnetometry, and low-temperature entropy measurements to probe these counterintuitive signatures.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a nonlocal Hamiltonian for a spin‑1/2 Heisenberg chain that supports unidirectional finite‑speed waves and exponentially small energies in the opposite direction, using an inverse thermodynamic Bethe ansatz. It predicts unusual thermodynamic signatures such as a logarithmically vanishing entropy with a golden ratio coefficient and proposes experimental probes via spin spectroscopy and magnetometry.

papers.title: FOORT: Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing
papers.authors: Daniel R. Mayerson, Seppe J. Staelens, Fabio Bacchini
papers.abstract: We present FOORT (Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing), an open C++ code for ray-tracing images of black holes and other compact objects in arbitrary spacetimes. FOORT is designed to offer flexibility and can handle horizons, naked singularities and numerical metrics, allowing it to ray-trace numerous different metrics including Kerr and other black holes, as well as horizonless objects such as fuzzballs and boson stars. New metrics, analytical or numerical, can be added with minimal effort, and geodesics are initialized at the camera without reference to conserved quantities, so no special structure of the metric is required. Besides the intensity observed from a geometrically and optically thin equatorial disk, FOORT is set up to track a number of diagnostics along each geodesic, such as the number of equatorial crossings and the radius of closest approach. Its adaptive mesh can refine the image on any of these diagnostics, efficiently resolving narrow features such as higher-order photon rings. Accompanying Python tools convert the output into images and interferometric visibility amplitudes. We describe the main features of the code, validate it against analytic results in the Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, demonstrate it on several non-Kerr metrics, and characterize its scaling with the number of OpenMP threads. FOORT is lightweight, requiring only C++17 and OpenMP, and has already been used in a number of studies of black hole and compact-object imaging. The code is publicly available in a GitHub repository.
papers.summary: FOORT is an open-source C++ framework for ray-tracing images of black holes and other compact objects in arbitrary spacetimes, supporting both analytic and numerical metrics and adaptive mesh refinement for fine features like photon rings. It offers diagnostics along geodesics and Python tools for image and visibility amplitude generation, and has been validated against Schwarzschild and Kerr solutions.

papers.title: Six-Loop Renormalization in Quantum Electrodynamics
papers.authors: Zeyu Li, Ming-xing Luo, Tong-Zhi Yang, Hua Xing Zhu
papers.abstract: We analytically compute the six-loop corrections to the scale evolution of the electric charge, fermion mass, and fermion field in quantum electrodynamics. The results are obtained in the $\MSbar$ scheme for an arbitrary number of equally charged fermions. They extend renormalization in quantum electrodynamics by one loop order and allow new tests of the behavior of perturbation theory at high orders. The methods developed here also open the way to six-loop computations of renormalization in quantum chromodynamics.
papers.summary: The paper presents an analytic six-loop computation of the renormalization group functions for the electric charge, fermion mass, and fermion field in QED within the μS scheme, extending previous five-loop results. It also outlines techniques that could be adapted to six-loop renormalization in QCD, offering a stringent test of perturbative convergence at high orders.

papers.title: Going beyond the standard quasiparticle picture: Entanglement spreading after quenching from highly entangled states
papers.abstract: The quasiparticle picture provides a quantitative description of entanglement spreading after quantum quenches in integrable systems. In interacting models, however, it relies on the assumption that the quench creates entangled pairs of quasiparticles, which is justified only for the so-called integrable initial states. Here we go beyond this setting by studying quenches in the XXZ spin chain from the $n$-rainbow states, a family of macroscopically homogeneous states formed by increasingly long-range Bell pairs, which are not integrable for $n>1$. The local stationary state after the quench approaches the infinite-temperature state as $n\to\infty$, with corrections of order $1/n$, as we show analytically. Nevertheless, in the noninteracting XX chain the quench produces entangled multiplets of $2n$ species of quasiparticles. Although interspecies correlations vanish as $1/n$, they strongly suppress the growth of the entanglement entropy, whose rate vanishes as $n\to\infty$. We capture this behaviour within a generalized quasiparticle picture. In the interacting XXZ chain, instead, time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (tDMRG) simulations show that the entanglement entropy grows at the rate at which thermodynamic entropy is exchanged across the cut. Within the time scales accessible to tDMRG, the data show no trace of the multiplet suppression. This holds both after homogeneous quenches and after joining the $n$-rainbow state with an infinite-temperature state, for which we conjecture a formula for the von Neumann entropy.
papers.summary: This study extends the quasiparticle framework to quenches from highly entangled rainbow states in the XXZ spin chain, revealing that in the noninteracting limit the entanglement growth is suppressed by interspecies correlations that vanish as 1/n. In the interacting case, tDMRG shows the entropy growth rate equals the thermodynamic entropy flux, with no evidence of multiplet suppression within accessible timescales.

papers.title: Exact model of a gravitational wave and electromagnetic radiation in DHOST gravity theory: wave solutions and testable effects
papers.abstract: Within an analytical non-perturbative framework based on a single exact model, the coupled dynamics of gravitational waves and high-frequency electromagnetic fields is investigated in General Relativity and DHOST gravity. Using an exact gravitational-wave spacetime in an isotropic (null) wave coordinate system, Maxwell's equations are integrated analytically. This analysis provides an exact non-perturbative confirmation from the full field equations that a gravitational wave acts as a waveguide, forming a propagation channel for electromagnetic radiation co-directional with the gravitational wave and generating an effective pure-radiation source. Applying this exact electrodynamic solution to the nonlinear field equations of DHOST class~Ia gravity reveals that the algebraic structure of the DHOST constraint equations enforces a modification of the electromagnetic-wave parameters. Based on this mechanism, an observationally testable effect of scalar frequency drift is derived, providing a direct way to discriminate between General Relativity and modified gravity theories even when their metric tensors share identical functional forms.
papers.summary: The paper presents an exact non‑perturbative solution for coupled gravitational and electromagnetic waves in DHOST gravity, showing that a gravitational wave can act as a waveguide for co‑directional EM radiation and predicts a scalar frequency drift as a testable signature. This result offers a potential observational discriminant between General Relativity and modified gravity theories with identical metric forms.

papers.title: On JT boundary algebras
papers.abstract: We construct the canonical boundary algebras of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter. For a nonempty finite or countable family of species with lowest weights greater than one half, the two boundary algebras are mutual commutants and nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ factors. Their nonzero finite corners are nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. The construction uses bounded heat-regularized fields and a Hilbert algebra, which gives a faithful normal semifinite trace without a path-integral argument. The weight restriction is sharp: elementary point fields remain unbounded after positive heat regularization when $0<d\leq1/2$. For one massless scalar, specified bounded observables and normal states have a high energy limit described by a hyperfinite continuous core. We explain why this limit does not preserve the nonhyperfiniteness of the exact algebra.
papers.summary: The paper constructs the canonical boundary operator algebras for Jackiw–Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter, showing that for species with lowest weights >1/2 the left and right algebras are mutual commutants and are non‑hyperfinite type II∞ factors, with finite corners being type II1. It further analyzes heat‑regularized bounded fields, the trace structure, and the high‑energy limit for a single massless scalar, illustrating how the exact non‑hyperfinite algebra reduces to a hyperfinite continuous core.

papers.title: Enhanced Early Structure from Axiodilatons & 21cm Observations
papers.authors: Chan Youn Weon, Carsten van de Bruck, C. P. Burgess, Jeong Han Kim, Adam Smith
papers.abstract: Axiodilatons provide a promising unified model of the Dark Sector whose properties are motivated by the use of accidental approximate symmetries to embed the light fields needed for observations into well-motivated UV physics in a technically natural way. These models turn out to help ameliorate many current puzzles in $\Lambda$CDM phenomenology (e.g. the Hubble tension and the evidence for evolving Dark Energy) `for free' despite not being designed for that purpose. We here explore in more detail another serendipitous feature of these models: their tendency to enhance early structure formation, in a way that seems suggestive given the accumulating evidence for structure arising earlier than expected in $\Lambda$CDM. Since early structure growth is the cleanest to study we explore in detail the expected 21cm signal produced by axiodilaton models, using the same parameter choices that improve agreement with observations elsewhere in cosmology. For fixed astrophysics, we forecast that SKA1-Low could distinguish dilaton couplings as small as a few times $10^{-2}$ from $\Lambda$CDM at $2\sigma$, mainly because of the earlier formation of structure. We provide complete derivations of the mass dependence of the relevant cosmological observables, including how dilaton-dependent baryon and electron masses affect the hyperfine transition, the Ly$\alpha$ coupling, X-ray heating and ionization during cosmic dawn and the epoch of reionization. We provide details of radiative transfer, atomic physics and the equations governing the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic medium.
papers.summary: This paper studies how axiodilaton fields can enhance early structure formation and produce distinctive 21cm signatures, potentially resolving tensions in ΛCDM. It provides detailed calculations of how dilaton couplings modify baryon and electron masses, affecting hyperfine transitions, Lyα coupling, X-ray heating, and reionization, and forecasts SKA1-Low sensitivity.

papers.title: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.
papers.summary: This paper establishes a precise link between periods of a Calabi–Yau threefold and critical values of a weight‑four modular L‑function, using a rational projector onto a $(3,0)+(0,3)$ Hodge summand. The authors then translate this arithmetic relation into a genus‑zero Gromov–Witten partition identity for the Fermat sextic, offering a new bridge between number theory and topological string theory.

papers.title: Radiative stability of species-separated Kaluza--Klein spectra in warped geometry
papers.authors: M. A. Anacleto, F. A. Brito, E. Passos, Joao R. L. Santos, J. A. V. Campos, I. E. L. M. Santana
papers.abstract: Species-dependent fifth-direction lightcones, generated by scalar-gradient operators, can separate gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein (KK) scales in a warped extra dimension, as recently shown by Randall and Riojas. In this work, we study whether this separation survives quantum corrections. Quark loops can only move the gluon speed within the interval spanned by the bare speeds. Gluon exchange pulls the quark speed toward the gluon speed, with a one-loop coefficient strongly enhanced by fifth-component exchange when the gluon is the slow species. We set the size of this effect using the strong-coupling estimates for a light-gluon benchmark, where a $5.5$~TeV gluon sits below quark partners at $10.74$~TeV. Within the effective theory, the Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes then correct the quark speed at order one. That correction is several times larger than the mass ordering can absorb, so the light-gluon ordering has no perturbative protection. The reverse benchmark, with slow quarks and a heavy gluon, keeps its ordering roughly ten times more robust.
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether the species-dependent lightcone separation of gauge and fermion Kaluza–Klein scales in a warped extra dimension, as proposed by Randall and Riojas, remains stable under quantum corrections. The authors find that quark loop corrections can significantly shift the gluon speed, destroying the light‑gluon ordering unless the gluon is the slow species, while the reverse scenario is more robust.

papers.title: Integrable Singularity Black Holes without Inner Horizons in Asymptotically Safe Inspired Gravity and NFW Dark Matter Effects
papers.abstract: We investigate an alternative ultraviolet (UV) structure for Renormalization Group improved (RG) black holes within a phenomenological framework inspired by asymptotically safe gravity. In several regular RG constructions, regularity at the origin is associated with a dS core and an additional inner horizon, raising issues of spacetime predictability and possible mass inflation instabilities. Motivated by this problem, we relate the RG scale to the radially weighted effective quantum gravitational source entering the volume integrand of the quantum corrected Ricci scalar. This prescription yields a Bessel type running Newton coupling with $G_I(r)\sim r$ in the UV, rather than the usual $G(r)\sim r^3$ behavior, and supports an integrable central singularity. The inner branch is matched through the Israel Darmois conditions to an exterior RG solution with $G_{II}\to G_0$ in the infrared, where $G_0$ is the Newton constant. Within the numerical range investigated, the resulting geometry has a single event horizon and no additional inner horizon. We then incorporate an NFW dark matter distribution coupled to the same running coupling. Since $\rho_{\rm NFW}\sim r^{-1}$ while $G_I(r)\sim r$ near the origin, the effective matter contribution entering the field equations remains finite, producing a cored effective behavior without modifying the NFW profile by hand. The gravitational decoupling algorithm keeps the quantum gravitational and dark matter sectors separately conserved within the same geometry. For the configurations considered, the NFW sector shifts the event horizon while preserving the single horizon structure. Thus, the same running coupling governs both the integrable UV black hole geometry and the softening of the central gravitational response of the NFW source.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a new RG‑improved black hole model with a Bessel‑type running Newton coupling that yields an integrable singularity and a single event horizon, avoiding inner horizons. It also couples an NFW dark matter profile to the same running coupling, producing a cored effective matter distribution without altering the NFW shape.

papers.title: The three-loop QCD helicity amplitudes for $V$+jet production at hadron colliders in full color
papers.authors: Thomas Gehrmann, Petr Jakub\v{c}\'{i}k, Andreas von Manteuffel, Cesare Carlo Mella, Lorenzo Tancredi
papers.abstract: We compute the three-loop Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) corrections to the production of a vector boson $V=Z,W^\pm,\gamma^*$ and a jet in quark-antiquark annihilation and its kinematic crossings, retaining full dependence on the number of colors. By expressing the infrared-finite remainders in terms of a small set of rational and special functions, we find that the amplitudes live in a strongly restricted function space, compared to the full space of the related Feynman integrals. We provide fast and reliable evaluation in all kinematic regions using numerical transport.
papers.summary: This paper presents the first complete three-loop QCD corrections to vector boson plus jet production in hadron collisions, providing infrared-finite remainders expressed in a restricted function space. The authors deliver fast numerical evaluation across all kinematic regimes, enabling precision phenomenology for LHC processes.

papers.title: Universal Theory of Strange and Bad Metals from Spatially Random Interactions with Underdamped Quantum-Critical Bosons
papers.abstract: One of the most important challenges in condensed matter physics is understanding the macroscopic properties of strange metals, particularly why their resistivity remains linear in temperature over several decades. We propose that a (2+1)d theory of fermions coupled to underdamped quantum-critical bosons through a spatially disordered interaction provides this long-sought-after theoretical explanation. The key novelty of our work is to establish the appropriate separation of scales so that the bosons are underdamped. Using this framework, we obtain two distinct forms for the fermionic self-energy: a conformal-limit solution, $\Sigma\sim\sqrt{\omega}$, and a marginal Fermi-liquid solution, $\Sigma\sim\omega\log(1/\omega)$, corresponding to regimes above and below the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit, respectively. These solutions produce Planckian scattering, exhibit exact $T$-linear resistivity, $\omega/T$ scaling in the optical conductivity, as well as $\sim T\log(1/T)$ heat capacity at low temperatures. Moreover, our theory naturally unifies strange- and bad-metal phenomena within a single framework, suggesting that we are now approaching a new epoch in understanding the physics of strongly correlated matter.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a (2+1)d model of fermions coupled to underdamped quantum‑critical bosons with spatially random interactions to explain linear‑T resistivity in strange metals. It finds two self‑energy regimes—conformal‑like $Sigmasimsqrt{omega}$ above the MIR limit and marginal Fermi‑liquid $Sigmasimomegalog(1/omega)$ below—yielding Planckian scattering, $omega/T$ scaling, and $Tlog T$ heat capacity.

papers.title: Crystalline Equivalence Principle for Anomalies
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic characterization of crystalline symmetry anomalies in bosonic lattice systems in (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions with a combination of crystalline and finite unitary internal symmetry. We construct anomaly indices of symmetry operators and derive their cocycle conditions and coboundary ambiguities. For generalized crystalline symmetries combining permutations of onsite Hilbert spaces with quantum cellular automata, anomaly indices take values in $H^3(B\widetilde \Gamma,U(1)_r)$ and $H^4(B\widetilde \Gamma,U(1)_r)$ respectively, where $\widetilde \Gamma$ is the total group of crystalline and internal symmetries, and the coefficient twist $r$ accounts for spatial orientation reversal. When crystalline symmetries act solely by permuting onsite Hilbert spaces, the anomaly classes restrict trivially to the spatial subgroup. These results establish a crystalline equivalence principle for bosonic anomalies at the microscopic level, without assuming a continuum description or emergent Lorentz invariance. We prove that a nontrivial total anomaly index obstructs any symmetric invertible phase. The framework incorporates modulated symmetries where spatial symmetries permute internal symmetries. Our results reproduce LSM and SPT--LSM constraints, with the latter illustrating how spectral-sequence differentials can trivialize candidate LSM anomaly indices.
papers.summary: The paper develops a microscopic framework for detecting crystalline symmetry anomalies in bosonic lattice systems, using group cohomology to define anomaly indices that capture both internal and spatial symmetries. It establishes a crystalline equivalence principle, showing that nontrivial total anomalies forbid symmetric invertible phases and reproduces known LSM and SPT–LSM constraints.

papers.title: Scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia: do they bind?
papers.abstract: We investigate the existence of molecular two-glueball bound states, so-called glueballonia, in pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory. We mainly concentrate on the scalar and pseudoscalar channels, thus studying scalar-scalar and scalar-pseudoscalar bound states, respectively. Near the onset of binding, when a bound state first appears just below threshold, a nonrelativistic framework is justified. We employ an attractive scalar-exchange Yukawa potential together with a smeared contact term contribution and determine the critical attraction required for binding. For two scalar glueballs, we use the scalar dilaton effective theory to determine the parameters of the non-relativistic potential: the Yukawa interaction is generated by t- and u-channels involving the exchange of one scalar glueball, while the repulsion emerges by the s-channel annihilation and contact interaction. Using lattice-YM input to fix the dilaton parameters, we find that the attraction is strong enough: the scalar glueballonium binds, and the result is quite robust with respect to parameter variations. In a minimal scalar-pseudoscalar extension, the Yukawa attraction is again given by the t-channel scalar glueball, while the crossed u-channel pseudoscalar exchange induces an attractive local contribution, making the pseudoscalar glueballonium also bind in pure gauge. Importantly, both the scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia are stable in the YM vacuum. Next, we briefly comment on the pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar, scalar-tensor, and tensor-tensor channels: all these channels are attractive too and could form bound states, which, however, would be unstable in pure YM due to decay into two lighter glueballs. Finally, as a cross-check, our formalism confirms that Higgs-Higgs bound state does not form.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia can form bound states in pure Yang‑Mills theory using a non‑relativistic Yukawa potential derived from dilaton effective theory, and confirms that these states are stable in the vacuum. It also shows that other glueball channels are attractive but unstable due to decay into lighter glueballs, and that a Higgs‑Higgs bound state does not form.

papers.title: Cubic Curvature Deformations to the Kerr Black Hole Shadow
papers.authors: Alireza Allahyari, Shinji Mukohyama, Yi Pang
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. Starting from a perturbatively corrected Kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. Using a Hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. We find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the Kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. In particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. We validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical Kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. Our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.
papers.summary: This work studies how cubic curvature terms in an effective field theory of gravity modify the shadow of a rotating black hole. By numerically integrating null geodesics in a perturbed Kerr metric, the authors quantify deviations in the shadow size and shape as functions of the higher‑curvature couplings, spin, and inclination, offering a potential observational test of beyond‑GR corrections.

papers.title: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
papers.authors: Shiyong Guo, Enrico Rinaldi, Jad C. Halimeh, Brian Swingle
papers.abstract: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model provides an analytically controlled setting for strongly interacting quantum dynamics and holography, but its fermionic formulation leads to nonlocal encoding overheads on qubit-based quantum processors. We study a U(1)-symmetric spin analogue of the complex SYK model, constructed from random charge-conserving $q$-spin interactions that are native to a qubit Hilbert space. In the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, the model reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK under the identification of chemical potential with magnetic field and charge density with magnetization. We investigate the finite-$N$, finite-$q$ regime using exact diagonalization. A U(1)-invariant ordering susceptibility increases with system size for $q = 2, 4$ but decreases for $q = 6$, while bulk-spectrum level statistics are consistent with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble at half filling and the Gaussian unitary ensemble in the adjacent magnetization sector. We further construct coupled-cluster chains and obtain domain-wall dynamics consistent with diffusive magnetization transport in a small-cluster regime accessible to matrix-product-state simulations. These results establish analytical benchmarks and finite-size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos, and magnetization transport in U(1)-symmetric spin-SYK models, and they motivate quantum simulation of the low-temperature, large-system regime, which remains difficult for classical methods.
papers.summary: This work introduces a qubit-friendly, U(1)-symmetric spin version of the complex SYK model that reproduces the large‑N, large‑q saddle‑point structure of the fermionic theory while preserving charge conservation. Using exact diagonalization and matrix‑product‑state simulations, the authors map out finite‑size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos (GOE/GUE statistics), and diffusive magnetization transport, offering benchmarks for future quantum simulations of the low‑temperature, large‑system regime.

papers.title: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
papers.abstract: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, N\'eel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.
papers.summary: This paper studies a 3D U(1) lattice gauge theory with a monopole enhancement term, showing that at large enhancement the monopoles form an antiferromagnetic crystal and deriving an effective sine‑Gordon description for dilute excitations. It also predicts first‑order and Ising‑type transitions in the monopole chemical potential and gauge coupling, and verifies these with numerical simulations.

papers.title: Critical behavior of the bosonized Schwinger model with uniform matrix product states
papers.abstract: Quantum electrodynamics in two spacetime dimensions, also known as the Schwinger model, admits a dual formulation in terms of a non-compact boson field. Using a Hamiltonian lattice discretization of the bosonized model, we compute the critical mass of the continuum Schwinger model at $\theta=\pi$. We numerically obtain the ground state on an infinite chain by the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm, preserving charge conjugation exactly. As a truncated basis for the local Hilbert space, we employ the oscillator basis that diagonalizes the one-site reduced density matrix of the free limit. We constrain the fitting functions for the continuum extrapolation using the Symanzik effective theory for lattice corrections. Our result for the critical mass, $(m/g)_c = 0.333\,555(5)$, agrees with recent staggered-fermion determinations at comparable precision.
papers.summary: The authors study the two-dimensional Schwinger model in its bosonized form, discretizing the theory on a lattice and employing the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm to obtain the infinite-chain ground state while preserving charge conjugation symmetry. They determine the critical fermion mass at θ=π to high precision, (m/g)_c = 0.333 555(5), and confirm agreement with recent staggered-fermion calculations, using Symanzik effective theory to control lattice artifacts.

papers.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
papers.abstract: We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$.   At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques.   Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.
papers.summary: This work constructs two-parameter Baxter Q‑operators for noncompact SL(2,ℂ) spin chains with open BC boundaries, showing that the transfer matrices factorize into one‑parameter Q‑operators and deriving a separation‑of‑variables framework that reduces the spectral problem to a Baxter equation. The authors use both algebraic identities and Feynman diagram techniques, offering new tools for integrable models with principal series representations.

papers.title: A Universal Law for Horizon Formation in Black Hole Mergers
papers.abstract: When two black holes merge, a common horizon appears around them as a single surface, which immediately splits into an outer and an inner one. We show that this event has a universal local form. Without any symmetry assumption, the two surfaces separate as $(t-t_*)^{1/2}$ along a single, everywhere positive mode and share a drift linear in $t-t_*$. Three numerical simulations, including an eccentric, precessing one, confirm the exponent to half a percent, and the reconstructed formation surface is marginally stable, as predicted.
papers.summary: The authors derive a universal scaling law for the birth of a common horizon during binary black hole mergers, showing that the outer and inner horizons separate as the square root of the time to the critical moment, independent of symmetry. Numerical simulations confirm the predicted exponent to within half a percent, and the resulting formation surface is marginally stable as expected.

papers.title: Probing the Molecular Nature of $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$ through Their Decays
papers.authors: Qing Lu, Dan Dan Feng, Cai Cheng, Yin Huang
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the molecular interpretations of $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$ by studying their strong decays within the effective Lagrangian approach. We consider two possible configurations for $D_{sJ}(2860)$: an $S$-wave $D_1K$ molecule and a $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecule, while treating $D_{s3}(2860)$ as a $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecule. By fitting the LHCb-measured angular distribution and decay widths in $B_s^0\to\bar{D}^0K^-\pi^+$, we determine the molecular coupling constants and cutoff parameter $\Lambda$. Using these parameters, we calculate the total decay widths and the ratios $R$ of the partial widths into the $D^*K$ and $DK$ channels. For $D_{sJ}(2860)$, the $S$-wave $D_1K$ assignment provides a slightly better description of the measured total width than the $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ assignment. However, the combined $D_1K$ and $D^*K^*$ assignments for $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$, respectively, are disfavored by the predicted $R_{D_{s3}(2860)}$, which exceeds the experimental upper limit. In contrast, assigning both states as $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecules yields good agreement with the measured $R_{D_{s3}(2860)}$ and predicts $R_{D_{sJ}(2860)}\simeq 1.26$--$1.29$. These results favor the $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecular interpretation for both states, which can be further tested through future measurements of $R_{D_{sJ}(2860)}$.
papers.summary: This study examines whether the excited charm‑strange mesons D_{sJ}(2860) and D_{s3}(2860) can be described as hadronic molecules, using effective Lagrangian techniques to fit LHCb data on decay widths and angular distributions. The authors find that treating both states as P‑wave D^*K^* molecules best reproduces the measured decay ratios, suggesting a molecular interpretation that can be tested by future measurements of the D_{sJ}(2860) decay ratio.
